_doc: HMTc Category 21 (Children's Toys, Arts, and Crafts) compiler config. Method v2.0, article form. Every numeric cell names EXPLICIT register ids; the compiler takes the strictest (min) over ids that share a basis. This category is regulated under two fundamentally different bases and the whole config is built to keep them apart. (A) MIGRATION / SOLUBLE: how much element transfers out of accessible toy material under the EN 71-3 / ISO 8124-3 0.07 M HCl 37 C stomach-acid extraction. Directive 2009/48/EC Annex II Part III point 13 splits this into three MATERIAL categories with three different limit sets — Category I dry/brittle/powder-like/pliable, Category II liquid or sticky, Category III scraped-off — ASTM F963-17 4.3.5 (mandatory in the US under CPSIA s.106 / 16 CFR 1250) sets soluble-element limits for surface coatings and accessible substrate, and Mexico's NOM-252-SSA1-2011 Table 1 (COFEPRIS, mandatory since 2012-08-13) sets bioavailable soluble-element limits for toy and school-article material in two scope tiers. All three state the same measured quantity, so all three are pooled in every strictest-selection; the ASTM and NOM-252 arsenic and mercury figures (25 and 60 mg/kg) bind over the Directive's Category III values, and NOM-252's 25 mg/kg chromium tier binds the modelling-clay and finger-paint rows. (B) TOTAL CONTENT: how much element the material contains — CPSIA s.101 total lead in children's-product substrate and in the dried paint film, Canada SOR/2011-17, SOR/2016-193 and SOR/2018-82/83, RoHS homogeneous-material limits for electrical and electronic equipment, and the REACH Annex XVII cadmium, organotin, Cr(VI)-in-leather and consumer-textile restrictions. EVERY row here publishes on basis (A) and carries basis (B) as a disclosed companion obligation, never as the published number. That direction was chosen because the migration regime spans the whole panel and is the stricter ceiling for lead and cadmium, whereas the content instruments are analyte-narrow and, for cadmium in paint (0.1 percent) and for every RoHS element, dramatically more permissive: publishing a content figure as the HMTc ceiling would replace a protective limit with a permissive one. The one content instrument that is stricter than its migration counterpart — Canada's 10 mg/kg total mercury in surface coating material — is disclosed on every mercury cell as a parallel obligation and surfaces in the audit scan as stricter-unselected, which is the audit working as designed rather than a missed anchor. A per-row basis_guard is kind-based on the extraction quantity: it admits the EU, ASTM and NOM-252 phrasings of acid-soluble migration while pinning the EU alternative to the material category or categories that row's scope actually spans, so a Category III value cannot silently anchor a Category I cell, an identically-based foreign migration row is not refused on phrasing, and no total-content row can resolve into a migration cell at all. iAs and MeHg are speciation-bounded not-material on every row (no toy instrument speciates arsenic or mercury; there is no methylation pathway in an article). Total chromium is a SCREEN taken over ASTM F963-17 and NOM-252 because the Toy Safety Directive sets Cr(III) and Cr(VI) limits and no total-chromium limit; the health-relevant species Cr(VI) carries its own published cell from the Directive. Total tin is likewise a SCREEN: the Directive's total-tin migration figure is dominated by benign inorganic tin, and the same instrument's organic-tin migration ceiling (0.9 / 0.2 / 12 mg/kg) is the health-relevant value and is a binding parallel obligation, disclosed on every tin cell and recorded as a register gap because those rows are not yet ingested. Antimony, barium and selenium are regulated by the toy-migration instruments but are not HMTc panel analytes; they are screened, not published.

_category.name: Children's Toys, Arts, and Crafts
_category.anchor: EU Toy Safety Directive 2009/48/EC Annex II Part III point 13 element-migration limits, matched per row to the EN 71-3 material category or categories the row's scope spans, taken jointly with the US ASTM F963-17 4.3.5 soluble-element limits (mandatory under CPSIA s.106 / 16 CFR 1250) and the Mexican NOM-252-SSA1-2011 Table 1 bioavailable soluble-element limits, which state the same measured quantity; the strictest value across that family binds each cell. Total-content law (CPSIA lead, RoHS, REACH Annex XVII, Canadian SOR coating limits) is carried as disclosed companion obligations and never as a published number.
_category.basis_family: Element MIGRATION from accessible toy material under the EN 71-3 / ISO 8124-3 0.07 M HCl 37 C stomach-acid extraction, expressed in mg/kg of toy material. Three sovereign instruments state this same quantity in three phrasings — Directive 2009/48/EC point 13 element migration, split by the Directive's three material categories; ASTM F963-17 4.3.5 soluble (migrated) element; and NOM-252-SSA1-2011 bioavailable soluble element — and all three are pooled in the strictest-selection. This is never conflated with total element CONTENT of the material (CPSIA s.101 lead, RoHS homogeneous material, REACH Annex XVII cadmium and organotin, the consumer-textile restriction, Canadian SOR total lead and total mercury in surface coating material), which is a different measured quantity; content instruments appear only as companion obligations in substantiation and are excluded from every cell by a per-row basis_guard anchored at the start of the register's basis string.
_category.method_label: HMTc Method v2.0 (government-limit default; strictest applicable sovereign maximum in the row's native basis, disclosed read-across where the exact cell is unregulated; never occurrence-derived). Category 21 publishes on the element-migration basis only, pooling the EU, US and Mexican migration instruments, with each row pinned to the EN 71-3 material category or categories its scope actually spans.
_category.method_note: READING THE STRICTER-UNSELECTED FLAGS. The audit scan compares every credible-regulator register row whose product scope matches this category against each cell's binding value and flags anything stricter that was not named. Three families of flag recur and each has a single standing answer. (1) SIBLING MATERIAL CATEGORIES. Directive 2009/48/EC Annex II Part III point 13 sets three limit sets for the same instrument, keyed to material form, and all three share a product scope, so on a Category III row the Category I and Category II values are always flagged as stricter. They are inapplicable: a limit for dry, brittle, powder-like or pliable material, or for liquid or sticky material, does not govern a material that must be scraped to be tested. Each row's basis_guard pins the EU alternative to the category or categories that row's scope actually spans, so a flagged sibling value could not have anchored the cell even if it had been named. Where a row's scope genuinely spans more than one material category (toys-stuffing-materials spans Categories I and III; art-craft-materials and toys-crafts-other span all three), every applicable category row IS named in gov_ids, the strictest binds, and the full candidate set is disclosed in the compiled record. (2) THE THREE-INSTRUMENT MIGRATION FAMILY. Directive 2009/48/EC point 13, ASTM F963-17 4.3.5 (mandatory in the US under CPSIA s.106 / 16 CFR 1250) and NOM-252-SSA1-2011 Table 1 state the same measured quantity in three phrasings, so all three are pooled and the strictest binds. For total arsenic and total mercury the ASTM and NOM-252 figures (25 and 60 mg/kg) are stricter than the Directive's Category III values (47 and 94 mg/kg) and therefore bind, which is also the position published on wiki/regulations/astm-f963-soluble-migration and wiki/regulations/eu-2009-48-toy-safety-migration-limits. A prior revision of this config rejected the ASTM figures on the argument that ASTM states its limits in the legacy lineage whose conformity rule subtracts a per-element analytical correction, making them looser as enforced. THAT ARGUMENT IS WITHDRAWN AS UNSUBSTANTIATED: the source cited for it documents the correction for ISO 8124-3:2020 and attributes none to ASTM, and its ASTM statement is a limit-value lineage claim that ends at F963-07, before the editions relied on. HMTc does not publish a ceiling above a CPSIA-mandatory figure on an unsubstantiated reading of a conformity clause. For total chromium, where the Directive sets Cr(III) and Cr(VI) limits and no total-chromium limit, ASTM and NOM-252 agree at 60 mg/kg for general toy material, and NOM-252's stricter 25 mg/kg tier for preschool school articles, modelling clay and finger paint binds the two rows whose scope names those forms. (3) CANADIAN TOTAL-MERCURY AND TOTAL-LEAD COATING LIMITS. SOR/2011-17 and SOR/2016-193 cap TOTAL mercury at 10 mg/kg and total lead at 90 mg/kg in surface coating material. Those are content ceilings, not migration ceilings; each is a real and binding parallel obligation, each is disclosed on the relevant cell, and each is excluded from the migration cells by the basis_guard because a content limit and a migration limit are different measured quantities. REGISTER GAPS RECORDED, NOT WORKED AROUND. Three sovereign values that would bear on this category are absent from data/evidence/regulatory_limits.csv and are returned for ingestion through the verified regulatory-fetch pathway rather than invented here: (a) the EU Cr(III) migration rows of Directive 2009/48/EC point 13 (verified absent — the register carries no Cr-III species at all); (b) the EU ORGANIC-TIN migration rows of the same point 13 table, 0.9 / 0.2 / 12 mg/kg for Categories I / II / III, which are the health-relevant tin ceiling and are 15 000 times lower than the Category III total-tin figure this config publishes as a screen; and (c) the REACH Annex XVII entry 27 nickel-release limit of 0.5 ug/cm2/week, which is a per-area release rate in a third basis. A fourth item previously recorded as a gap is withdrawn: the 25 mg/kg modelling-clay and finger-paint chromium value IS in the register, as the Mexican statutory row mx_nom252_2011_cr_total_preschool_clay_fingerpaint_25, and it now binds the two rows whose scope names those material forms. NOT CONVERTED INTO NUMBERS. The US LHAMA regime (15 U.S.C. 1277 / 16 CFR 1500.14(b)(8) via ASTM D-4236) is a chronic-hazard review and labelling duty with no numeric maximum level, and the mechanical requirements of EN 71-1 and ASTM F963-17 (small parts, magnet flux index, projectile kinetic energy, lid supports, balloon and marble warnings) are not metals limits. Neither is converted into a ceiling anywhere in this config.
_category.credible_note: MX (Secretaria de Salud / COFEPRIS) is admitted to the credible-regulator set for this category by governance ruling. NOM-252-SSA1-2011, mandatory since 2012-08-13, is Mexico's federal toy and school-article heavy-metals standard. Its Table 1 sets maximum bioavailable soluble-element limits for eight elements on the same acid-extraction quantity as EN 71-3 / ISO 8124-3 migration, in two scope tiers: any toy or school-article material except modelling clay and finger paint, and preschool school articles, modelling clay and finger paint. It is a federal instrument of general application enforced by COFEPRIS, not a sub-national or advisory measure, it carries its own Heavy Metal Index regulation page (wiki/regulations/mexico-nom-252-ssa1-2011-toy-school-article-metals), and the regulation pages for BOTH instruments this category otherwise relies on already name it as a member of the toy-migration family whose strictest value binds. Admitting MX is what lets the audit scan see its twelve statutory rows: before this change the scan gated on the default credible set, so NOM-252 was invisible to it and three of its rows were stricter than values this config published (arsenic 25 mg/kg and mercury 60 mg/kg against 47 and 94; modelling-clay and finger-paint total chromium 25 mg/kg against 60). The addition can only tighten: NOM-252 enters the strictest-selection on the same footing as every other named instrument and never sets a ceiling above one already published.

toys-painted.name: General toys with paint/surface coatings
toys-painted.native_basis: element migration from scraped-off toy material (Directive 2009/48/EC Annex II Part III point 13, Category III; EN 71-3 / ISO 8124-3 0.07 M HCl 37 C extraction), mg/kg of toy material
toys-painted.native_basis_label: element MIGRATION from scraped-off toy material (EN 71-3 Category III, mg/kg of material) — a migration ceiling, not a total-content ceiling
toys-painted.scope_note: Toys bearing an accessible applied paint, varnish, lacquer, printing ink, applied sticker, film or other surface coating. The coating itself is the certified material for this row; the toy body underneath is certified under toys-substrate-materials. EN 71-3 clause 9.1 treats coatings of paint, varnish, lacquer, printing ink and polymer as scraped-off material (Category III). Total-lead-in-paint law is the most-cited instrument for painted toys and is carried as a companion CONTENT obligation on every cell, never as the published migration number.
toys-painted.material: Cured surface coating: paint, varnish, lacquer, enamel, printing ink, screen-print, hot-stamp foil, applied decal, sticker and film.
toys-painted.components: Sample each distinct colour and each distinct coating system separately (a multi-colour print is multiple test portions). Scrape the coating to substrate over at least 100 mg per colour without entraining substrate. Sample the coating on any small part or removable accessory separately. Record coating thickness and whether the coating is accessible before and after the use-and-abuse conditioning of ASTM F963-17 8.5 / EN 71-1.
toys-painted.audit_scope: toy|children'?s (product|article|jewell?ery)|school.?article|student article|surface coating|accessible part|coated with a material
toys-painted.basis_guard: ^(element migration from [^;]*toy material \(Category (III)\)|soluble \(migrated\) element from |bioavailable soluble element from )
toys-painted.basis_guard_note: This row's material is tested by scraping (cured coatings, polymers, elastomers, textiles, wood, paper, glass, ceramic and metal), which is EN 71-3 Category III, so the EU alternative in the guard is pinned to Category III alone. The guard is kind-based on the extraction quantity rather than a literal-phrase whitelist: it admits any register row whose basis BEGINS with element migration from toy material of an admitted material category, with soluble (migrated) element, or with bioavailable soluble element — the three phrasings the EU, US and Mexican migration instruments use for the same 0.07 M HCl acid-extraction quantity — and it will admit a future sovereign migration row phrased differently again only if that row states the same quantity. Anchored at the start of the basis string, it rejects every total-CONTENT phrasing carried in the register (CPSIA total lead content by weight, lead content in accessible part, RoHS homogeneous material, REACH Annex XVII cadmium and organotin content, total cadmium and total lead in children's jewellery, total dry weight of leather, the consumer-textile cadmium restriction, dried-sample and non-volatile coating content, and removable sticker or film content), so no content limit can be resolved into a migration cell. The earlier literal-phrase form was over-restrictive in the one direction that mattered: it refused Mexico's identically-based NOM-252 bioavailable rows even when they were named, and because the guard only fires on ids actually named in a cell, a guard-driven exclusion narrowed the strictest-selection pool silently instead of reporting itself. One soluble-basis register row remains outside the guard on phrasing — Minnesota ch. 347 soluble cadmium in children's jewellery, 75 mg/kg (mn_ch347_2010_cd_childrens_jewelry_75ppm) — and it is neither stricter than any value published on this row nor inside the credible-regulator set (US-MN is a state measure carrying its own federal-supersession caveat).

Pb.basis_label: element MIGRATION from scraped-off toy material (EN 71-3 Category III, mg/kg of material) — a migration ceiling, not a total-content ceiling
Pb.label: Strictest applicable sovereign lead-migration maximum for Category III (scraped-off) toy material, taken across the whole migration family: Directive 2009/48/EC point 13 Category III 23 mg/kg (binding), ASTM F963-17 4.3.5 soluble lead 90 mg/kg (mandatory in the US under CPSIA s.106), and NOM-252-SSA1-2011 Table 1 bioavailable lead 90 mg/kg (MX).
Pb.substantiation: All named ids state one measured quantity — the acid-soluble element that migrates from accessible toy material under the EN 71-3 / ISO 8124-3 0.07 M HCl 37 C extraction, which NOM-252-SSA1-2011 calls bioavailable soluble element — so the strictest-selection is basis-clean. The Directive's Category III value binds at 23 mg/kg; the ASTM and NOM-252 rows are named so the strictest-selection covers the complete applicable family rather than a subset, and both are looser than the binding value. Total-lead CONTENT law runs in parallel on a different basis and is a companion obligation, not this cell's ceiling: CPSIA s.101 caps total lead at 100 mg/kg in any accessible children's-product substrate (cpsia_pb_childrens_product_substrate_100ppm) and at 90 mg/kg in the dried paint film (cpsia_pb_surface_coating_90ppm); Canada SOR/2016-193 and SOR/2011-17 set 90 mg/kg total lead in surface coating material and in applied stickers and films; Canada SOR/2018-83 sets 90 mg/kg total lead in accessible parts. HMTc requires conformity with both the migration ceiling published here and those content ceilings; the two are different measured quantities and are never combined into one number.

Cd.basis_label: element MIGRATION from scraped-off toy material (EN 71-3 Category III, mg/kg of material) — a migration ceiling, not a total-content ceiling
Cd.label: Strictest applicable sovereign cadmium-migration maximum for Category III (scraped-off) toy material, taken across the whole migration family: Directive 2009/48/EC point 13 Category III 17 mg/kg (binding), ASTM F963-17 4.3.5 soluble cadmium 75 mg/kg, and NOM-252-SSA1-2011 Table 1 bioavailable cadmium 75 mg/kg (MX).
Cd.substantiation: All named ids state one measured quantity — the acid-soluble element that migrates from accessible toy material under the EN 71-3 / ISO 8124-3 0.07 M HCl 37 C extraction, which NOM-252-SSA1-2011 calls bioavailable soluble element — so the strictest-selection is basis-clean. The Directive's Category III value binds at 17 mg/kg; the ASTM and NOM-252 rows are named for completeness of the applicable family and are looser. REACH Annex XVII entry 23 as amended by Regulation (EU) 494/2011 restricts cadmium by total CONTENT (0.01 percent in listed polymers and in jewellery metal parts, 0.1 percent in paint and painted articles). Those are content ceilings on a different measured quantity and are far more permissive than the migration ceiling published here; they are recorded as companion obligations and are deliberately NOT used to set this cell, because publishing a 0.1-percent paint-content figure as the HMTc cadmium ceiling would replace a protective migration limit with a permissive content limit.

tAs.basis_label: acid-soluble / MIGRATED element from accessible toy material (EN 71-3 / ISO 8124-3 0.07 M HCl, 37 C, mg/kg of material). The three instruments in this family state the same measured quantity in three phrasings: Directive 2009/48/EC point 13 element migration, which IS split by material category and whose applicable member here is the Category III (scraped-off material) value; ASTM F963-17 4.3.5 soluble (migrated) element; and NOM-252-SSA1-2011 bioavailable soluble element. The ASTM and NOM-252 limits are not EN 71-3 material-category scoped, so where one of them binds, the published ceiling carries no material-category qualifier. A migration ceiling, not a total-content ceiling.
tAs.label: Strictest applicable sovereign total-arsenic migration maximum for Category III (scraped-off) toy material, taken across the whole migration family: ASTM F963-17 4.3.5 soluble arsenic 25 mg/kg (mandatory in the US under CPSIA s.106 / 16 CFR 1250) and NOM-252-SSA1-2011 Table 1 bioavailable arsenic 25 mg/kg (MX) both bind at 25 mg/kg, below the Directive's point 13 Category III value of 47 mg/kg.
tAs.substantiation: All named ids state one measured quantity — the acid-soluble element that migrates from accessible toy material under the EN 71-3 / ISO 8124-3 0.07 M HCl 37 C extraction, which NOM-252-SSA1-2011 calls bioavailable soluble element — so the strictest-selection is basis-clean. Two of the three instruments set 25 mg/kg against the Directive's 47 mg/kg, so 25 mg/kg is the published ceiling and HMTc applies it to the laboratory's analytical result as reported. A previous revision of this config published the Directive's looser Category III figure instead, on the argument that ASTM states its soluble limits in the legacy EN 71-3 / ISO 8124-3 lineage, in which conformity is judged against an analytical-correction-adjusted result, so that ASTM's nominal figure is looser than the Directive's once both are put on a raw-result footing. THAT ARGUMENT IS WITHDRAWN AS UNSUBSTANTIATED. The only repository artifact cited for it, wiki/sources/iso2020-8124-3-toy-migration-elements.md, documents the Table 2 analytical correction for ISO 8124-3:2020 and says of ASTM only that F963 4.3 sits in the same lineage and used the legacy EN 71-3 limits unchanged through F963-07 — a limit-VALUE lineage statement that expressly ends before the F963-08 and later editions this cell relies on, and it attributes no analytical correction to ASTM at all. The register row's own notes record only that the values are unchanged across F963-08/-11/-16/-17/-23. HMTc does not publish a ceiling above a figure made mandatory by CPSIA s.106 / 16 CFR 1250 on an unsubstantiated reading of a conformity clause. If ASTM F963-17 4.3.5 / 8.3 is later ingested as a source page that quotes the conformity-decision rule and it does specify a correction, the question may be reopened on that record; until then the stricter figure binds, which is also the position already published on wiki/regulations/astm-f963-soluble-migration and wiki/regulations/eu-2009-48-toy-safety-migration-limits. Arsenic is limited as the TOTAL element by every instrument in the family; inorganic arsenic has no migration counterpart and is handled on the iAs cell.

not_material.rationale: No sovereign toy-safety instrument sets an inorganic-arsenic limit. Directive 2009/48/EC Annex II Part III point 13, EN 71-3, ISO 8124-3:2020 Table 1, ASTM F963-17 4.3.5 and NOM-252-SSA1-2011 Table 1 all regulate TOTAL arsenic migration from toy material; inorganic arsenic is a dietary speciation with no article-migration counterpart. Arsenic in a cured paint, varnish, lacquer, printing-ink or polymer surface coating is bounded by the published total-arsenic migration ceiling by identity (iAs <= tAs), so a separate inorganic-arsenic ceiling would add no control.
not_material.reference_method: Total-arsenic migration on this row's EN 71-3 material category (0.07 M HCl, 37 C, 1 h agitation + 1 h standing, 0.45 um filtration, ICP-MS). No reflex arsenic speciation is defined for toy materials; HMTc requires a reflex investigation of the arsenic source whenever total-arsenic migration exceeds 50 percent of the published ceiling.
not_material.regulatory_basis: Directive 2009/48/EC Annex II Part III point 13 (arsenic, total element, three material categories); ASTM F963-17 4.3.5 soluble arsenic (total element), mandatory in the US under CPSIA s.106; ISO 8124-3:2020 Table 1 (arsenic, total element). NOM-252-SSA1-2011 Table 1 (arsenic, total element, both scope tiers), mandatory in Mexico since 2012-08-13. None of the four speciates arsenic.
not_material.jurisdictions_checked: EU (2009/48/EC as amended), UK (retained TSD / Toys (Safety) Regulations 2011), US (CPSIA s.106 / 16 CFR 1250 / ASTM F963-17), CA (SOR/2011-17, SOR/2016-193, SOR/2018-83), AU-NZ, CODEX, MX (NOM-252-SSA1-2011), international (ISO 8124-3:2020)

tHg.basis_label: acid-soluble / MIGRATED element from accessible toy material (EN 71-3 / ISO 8124-3 0.07 M HCl, 37 C, mg/kg of material). The three instruments in this family state the same measured quantity in three phrasings: Directive 2009/48/EC point 13 element migration, which IS split by material category and whose applicable member here is the Category III (scraped-off material) value; ASTM F963-17 4.3.5 soluble (migrated) element; and NOM-252-SSA1-2011 bioavailable soluble element. The ASTM and NOM-252 limits are not EN 71-3 material-category scoped, so where one of them binds, the published ceiling carries no material-category qualifier. A migration ceiling, not a total-content ceiling.
tHg.label: Strictest applicable sovereign total-mercury migration maximum for Category III (scraped-off) toy material, taken across the whole migration family: ASTM F963-17 4.3.5 soluble mercury 60 mg/kg (mandatory in the US under CPSIA s.106 / 16 CFR 1250) and NOM-252-SSA1-2011 Table 1 bioavailable mercury 60 mg/kg (MX) both bind at 60 mg/kg, below the Directive's point 13 Category III value of 94 mg/kg.
tHg.substantiation: All named ids state one measured quantity — the acid-soluble element that migrates from accessible toy material under the EN 71-3 / ISO 8124-3 0.07 M HCl 37 C extraction, which NOM-252-SSA1-2011 calls bioavailable soluble element — so the strictest-selection is basis-clean. Two of the three instruments set 60 mg/kg against the Directive's 94 mg/kg, so 60 mg/kg is the published ceiling and HMTc applies it to the laboratory's analytical result as reported. A previous revision of this config published the Directive's looser Category III figure instead, on the argument that ASTM states its soluble limits in the legacy EN 71-3 / ISO 8124-3 lineage, in which conformity is judged against an analytical-correction-adjusted result, so that ASTM's nominal figure is looser than the Directive's once both are put on a raw-result footing. THAT ARGUMENT IS WITHDRAWN AS UNSUBSTANTIATED. The only repository artifact cited for it, wiki/sources/iso2020-8124-3-toy-migration-elements.md, documents the Table 2 analytical correction for ISO 8124-3:2020 and says of ASTM only that F963 4.3 sits in the same lineage and used the legacy EN 71-3 limits unchanged through F963-07 — a limit-VALUE lineage statement that expressly ends before the F963-08 and later editions this cell relies on, and it attributes no analytical correction to ASTM at all. The register row's own notes record only that the values are unchanged across F963-08/-11/-16/-17/-23. HMTc does not publish a ceiling above a figure made mandatory by CPSIA s.106 / 16 CFR 1250 on an unsubstantiated reading of a conformity clause. If ASTM F963-17 4.3.5 / 8.3 is later ingested as a source page that quotes the conformity-decision rule and it does specify a correction, the question may be reopened on that record; until then the stricter figure binds, which is also the position already published on wiki/regulations/astm-f963-soluble-migration and wiki/regulations/eu-2009-48-toy-safety-migration-limits. Separately, Canada SOR/2016-193 and SOR/2011-17 set 10 mg/kg TOTAL mercury in surface coating material and in applied stickers and films. That is a total-content ceiling on the coating, a different measured quantity from migration, and it is stricter than the migration ceiling published here. It is carried as a companion obligation rather than substituted into this cell, and HMTc requires conformity with BOTH: an article whose coating carries more than 10 mg/kg total mercury does not certify, whatever its migration result. AUDIT ANSWER — NOM-252 PRESCHOOL TIER. The audit scan flags NOM-252-SSA1-2011's stricter mercury tier (25 mg/kg, mx_nom252_2011_thg_preschool_clay_fingerpaint_25) as unselected. It is inapplicable to this row: that tier is scoped to preschool SCHOOL ARTICLES, modelling clay and finger paint, and NOM-252's general tier expressly covers any toy or school-article material EXCEPT modelling clay and finger paint, so a toy of this row's description sits in the general tier at 60 mg/kg. The stricter tier is adopted where the row's material genuinely is a school-craft, modelling-clay or finger-paint form: it binds on art-craft-materials, toys-crafts-other and toys-pompoms-fibrous-craft.

not_material.rationale: Methylmercury is produced by microbial methylation in aquatic systems and reaches humans by diet. a cured paint, varnish, lacquer, printing-ink or polymer surface coating carries no methylation pathway and no dietary route, and no sovereign toy instrument sets a methylmercury limit: every toy mercury limit (2009/48/EC point 13, ASTM F963-17 4.3.5, ISO 8124-3:2020, NOM-252-SSA1-2011, Canada SOR/2011-17 and SOR/2016-193) is on total mercury. Any organomercury fraction is bounded by the published total-mercury migration ceiling by identity (MeHg <= tHg).
not_material.reference_method: Total-mercury migration on this row's EN 71-3 material category (0.07 M HCl, 37 C, CV-AAS or ICP-MS). Methylmercury speciation is run only on reflex, whenever total-mercury migration exceeds 50 percent of the published ceiling.
not_material.regulatory_basis: Directive 2009/48/EC Annex II Part III point 13 (mercury, total element); ASTM F963-17 4.3.5 soluble mercury (total element); ISO 8124-3:2020 Table 1 (mercury, total element); Canada SOR/2011-17 and SOR/2016-193 (total mercury in surface coating material). NOM-252-SSA1-2011 Table 1 (mercury, total element, both scope tiers). None speciates mercury.
not_material.jurisdictions_checked: EU (2009/48/EC as amended), UK (retained TSD / Toys (Safety) Regulations 2011), US (CPSIA s.106 / 16 CFR 1250 / ASTM F963-17), CA (SOR/2011-17, SOR/2016-193), AU-NZ, CODEX, MX (NOM-252-SSA1-2011), international (ISO 8124-3:2020)

Ni.basis_label: element MIGRATION from scraped-off toy material (EN 71-3 Category III, mg/kg of material) — a migration ceiling, not a total-content ceiling
Ni.label: EU Toy Safety Directive nickel migration maximum for Category III (scraped-off) toy material.
Ni.substantiation: The Toy Safety Directive is the only credible sovereign instrument that sets a numeric nickel ceiling for toy material; ASTM F963-17 and ISO 8124-3:2020 do not regulate nickel at all, and NOM-252-SSA1-2011 Table 1 regulates antimony, arsenic, barium, cadmium, total chromium, lead, mercury and selenium and sets no nickel limit, so admitting MX to the credible-regulator set does not add a candidate to this cell. The Directive's nickel figures are permissive relative to the other panel analytes and HMTc publishes them as written rather than substituting an occurrence-derived or invented value. REACH Annex XVII entry 27 additionally caps nickel RELEASE from articles in prolonged skin contact at 0.5 ug/cm2/week; that is a per-area release rate in a third basis, it is not represented in the register, and it is recorded as a companion obligation and a register gap rather than converted into a mg/kg figure here.

Sn.basis_label: element MIGRATION from scraped-off toy material (EN 71-3 Category III, mg/kg of material) — a migration ceiling, not a total-content ceiling

Sn.substantiation: Directive 2009/48/EC Annex II Part III point 13 is the only instrument in the register that sets a numeric tin ceiling for toy material: ASTM F963-17 and ISO 8124-3:2020 do not regulate tin, and NOM-252-SSA1-2011 Table 1 regulates antimony, arsenic, barium, cadmium, total chromium, lead, mercury and selenium and sets no tin limit, so admitting MX to the credible-regulator set does not add a candidate to this cell. The register holds only the Directive's three TOTAL-tin rows. The instrument itself sets TWO tin lines on the same migration basis: total tin (15 000 / 3 750 / 180 000 mg/kg for Categories I / II / III) and organic tin (0.9 / 0.2 / 12 mg/kg), the latter reproduced from the point 13 table on wiki/regulations/eu-2009-48-toy-safety-migration-limits. A prior revision of this cell asserted that the Directive is the only credible sovereign instrument setting a numeric tin ceiling and disclosed only the REACH Annex XVII entry 20 organotin CONTENT restriction; that statement was wrong by omission, because it left the reader unaware that the same instrument caps organic tin at 12 mg/kg for this row's scraped-off (Category III) material while this cell publishes 180 000 mg/kg. The organic-tin migration rows are a recorded REGISTER GAP returned for ingestion through the verified regulatory-fetch pathway; once ingested, this row should gain a published organotin cell beside the total-tin screen, exactly as chromium carries a published Cr(VI) cell beside its total-chromium screen. Organotin is additionally restricted by REACH Annex XVII entry 20 on a total-CONTENT basis (0.1 percent as tin for dibutyltin, and for skin-contact and childcare articles dioctyltin); that is a different measured quantity and is a further companion obligation, not this cell's anchor.
Sn.screen_note: SCREEN, not a protective standalone ceiling. The published figure is TOTAL tin migration: 180 000 mg/kg of material, which is dominated by benign inorganic tin. The health-relevant tin fraction is organotin, and the SAME instrument on the SAME migration basis (Directive 2009/48/EC Annex II Part III point 13) sets a separate organic-tin migration ceiling of 0.9 mg/kg for Category I, 0.2 mg/kg for Category II and 12 mg/kg for Category III — for this row's scraped-off (Category III) material that is 12 mg/kg, orders of magnitude below the total-tin figure. Those organic-tin rows are not in data/evidence/regulatory_limits.csv, so no organotin cell can be compiled and none is invented; the total-tin value is therefore recorded as a screen and the organic-tin ceiling is a BINDING PARALLEL OBLIGATION of equal standing, not an optional companion. The total-tin result triggers and bounds organotin determination, never substitutes for it.

Al.basis_label: element MIGRATION from scraped-off toy material (EN 71-3 Category III, mg/kg of material) — a migration ceiling, not a total-content ceiling

The 2019/1922 amendment already tightened these values by roughly 2.5x; HMTc publishes the amended figures as written.

Cr.basis_label: acid-soluble / MIGRATED element from accessible toy material (EN 71-3 / ISO 8124-3 0.07 M HCl, 37 C, mg/kg of material). The three instruments in this family state the same measured quantity in three phrasings: Directive 2009/48/EC point 13 element migration, which IS split by material category and whose applicable member here is the Category III (scraped-off material) value; ASTM F963-17 4.3.5 soluble (migrated) element; and NOM-252-SSA1-2011 bioavailable soluble element. The ASTM and NOM-252 limits are not EN 71-3 material-category scoped, so where one of them binds, the published ceiling carries no material-category qualifier. A migration ceiling, not a total-content ceiling.
Cr.screen_note: SCREEN, not a protective standalone ceiling. Total chromium in toy material is dominated by benign Cr(III) from pigments, stainless components and tanned leather; the health-relevant species is Cr(VI), which carries its own published cell on this row. The total-chromium result is used to trigger and to bound Cr(VI) speciation, never as a substitute for it.
Cr.label: Total-chromium migration maximum taken over the two credible sovereign instruments that set one on this basis: ASTM F963-17 4.3.5 soluble total chromium 60 mg/kg (mandatory in the US under CPSIA s.106) and NOM-252-SSA1-2011 Table 1 bioavailable total chromium 60 mg/kg for toy or school-article material other than modelling clay and finger paint (MX). Both agree at 60 mg/kg. Recorded as a SCREEN, not a protective standalone ceiling.
Cr.substantiation: The EU Toy Safety Directive splits chromium into Cr(III) and Cr(VI) and sets no TOTAL-chromium ceiling, so the total-chromium value is taken over the two credible sovereign instruments that do set one on the acid-soluble migration basis. Second, the claim that the ISO 8124-3:2020 modelling-clay and finger-paint chromium limits of 25 mg/kg were a register gap: the same 25 mg/kg value for the same two material forms IS in the register as the Mexican statutory row mx_nom252_2011_cr_total_preschool_clay_fingerpaint_25, and it now binds the rows it applies to. One genuine register gap remains against this cell and is recorded rather than worked around: the EU Cr(III) migration rows of Directive 2009/48/EC point 13 are absent from the register (verified — no Cr-III species exists anywhere in it) and are not invented here. AUDIT ANSWER — NOM-252 PRESCHOOL TIER. The audit scan flags NOM-252-SSA1-2011's stricter chromium tier (25 mg/kg, mx_nom252_2011_cr_total_preschool_clay_fingerpaint_25) as unselected. toys-substrate-materials.name: Toy substrate materials (accessible plastics/metals/woods/rubbers)

All are tested by scraping, which is EN 71-3 Category III.

toys-substrate-materials.audit_scope: toy|children'?s (product|article|jewell?ery)|school.?article|student article|surface coating|accessible part|coated with a material
toys-substrate-materials.basis_guard: ^(element migration from [^;]*toy material \(Category (III)\)|soluble \(migrated\) element from |bioavailable soluble element from )
toys-substrate-materials.basis_guard_note: This row's material is tested by scraping (cured coatings, polymers, elastomers, textiles, wood, paper, glass, ceramic and metal), which is EN 71-3 Category III, so the EU alternative in the guard is pinned to Category III alone. The guard is kind-based on the extraction quantity rather than a literal-phrase whitelist: it admits any register row whose basis BEGINS with element migration from toy material of an admitted material category, with soluble (migrated) element, or with bioavailable soluble element — the three phrasings the EU, US and Mexican migration instruments use for the same 0.07 M HCl acid-extraction quantity — and it will admit a future sovereign migration row phrased differently again only if that row states the same quantity. Anchored at the start of the basis string, it rejects every total-CONTENT phrasing carried in the register (CPSIA total lead content by weight, lead content in accessible part, RoHS homogeneous material, REACH Annex XVII cadmium and organotin content, total cadmium and total lead in children's jewellery, total dry weight of leather, the consumer-textile cadmium restriction, dried-sample and non-volatile coating content, and removable sticker or film content), so no content limit can be resolved into a migration cell. The earlier literal-phrase form was over-restrictive in the one direction that mattered: it refused Mexico's identically-based NOM-252 bioavailable rows even when they were named, and because the guard only fires on ids actually named in a cell, a guard-driven exclusion narrowed the strictest-selection pool silently instead of reporting itself. One soluble-basis register row remains outside the guard on phrasing — Minnesota ch. 347 soluble cadmium in children's jewellery, 75 mg/kg (mn_ch347_2010_cd_childrens_jewelry_75ppm) — and it is neither stricter than any value published on this row nor inside the credible-regulator set (US-MN is a state measure carrying its own federal-supersession caveat).

Pb.basis_label: element MIGRATION from scraped-off toy material (EN 71-3 Category III, mg/kg of material) — a migration ceiling, not a total-content ceiling

Pb.substantiation: All named ids state one measured quantity — the acid-soluble element that migrates from accessible toy material under the EN 71-3 / ISO 8124-3 0.07 M HCl 37 C extraction, which NOM-252-SSA1-2011 calls bioavailable soluble element — so the strictest-selection is basis-clean. The Directive's Category III value binds at 23 mg/kg; the ASTM and NOM-252 rows are named so the strictest-selection covers the complete applicable family rather than a subset, and both are looser than the binding value. Total-lead CONTENT law runs in parallel on a different basis and is a companion obligation, not this cell's ceiling: CPSIA s.101 caps total lead at 100 mg/kg in any accessible children's-product substrate (cpsia_pb_childrens_product_substrate_100ppm) and at 90 mg/kg in the dried paint film (cpsia_pb_surface_coating_90ppm); Canada SOR/2016-193 and SOR/2011-17 set 90 mg/kg total lead in surface coating material and in applied stickers and films; Canada SOR/2018-83 sets 90 mg/kg total lead in accessible parts. THAT ARGUMENT IS WITHDRAWN AS UNSUBSTANTIATED. The only repository artifact cited for it, wiki/sources/iso2020-8124-3-toy-migration-elements.md, documents the Table 2 analytical correction for ISO 8124-3:2020 and says of ASTM only that F963 4.3 sits in the same lineage and used the legacy EN 71-3 limits unchanged through F963-07 — a limit-VALUE lineage statement that expressly ends before the F963-08 and later editions this cell relies on, and it attributes no analytical correction to ASTM at all. not_material.reference_method: Total-arsenic migration on this row's EN 71-3 material category (0.07 M HCl, 37 C, 1 h agitation + 1 h standing, 0.45 um filtration, ICP-MS). not_material.jurisdictions_checked: EU (2009/48/EC as amended), UK (retained TSD / Toys (Safety) Regulations 2011), US (CPSIA s.106 / 16 CFR 1250 / ASTM F963-17), CA (SOR/2011-17, SOR/2016-193, SOR/2018-83), AU-NZ, CODEX, MX (NOM-252-SSA1-2011), international (ISO 8124-3:2020)

The 2019/1922 amendment already tightened these values by roughly 2.5x; HMTc publishes the amended figures as written.

toys-stuffed-bean-bag.components: Separate test portions for: outer face fabric (per colour), pile, embroidery and applique thread, printed or screen-printed areas, plastic eyes/noses/safety joints, ribbons and woven labels, zips and metal fasteners. toys-stuffed-bean-bag.audit_scope: toy|children'?s (product|article|jewell?ery)|school.?article|student article|surface coating|accessible part|coated with a material
toys-stuffed-bean-bag.basis_guard: ^(element migration from [^;]*toy material \(Category (III)\)|soluble \(migrated\) element from |bioavailable soluble element from )
toys-stuffed-bean-bag.basis_guard_note: This row's material is tested by scraping (cured coatings, polymers, elastomers, textiles, wood, paper, glass, ceramic and metal), which is EN 71-3 Category III, so the EU alternative in the guard is pinned to Category III alone. The guard is kind-based on the extraction quantity rather than a literal-phrase whitelist: it admits any register row whose basis BEGINS with element migration from toy material of an admitted material category, with soluble (migrated) element, or with bioavailable soluble element — the three phrasings the EU, US and Mexican migration instruments use for the same 0.07 M HCl acid-extraction quantity — and it will admit a future sovereign migration row phrased differently again only if that row states the same quantity. Anchored at the start of the basis string, it rejects every total-CONTENT phrasing carried in the register (CPSIA total lead content by weight, lead content in accessible part, RoHS homogeneous material, REACH Annex XVII cadmium and organotin content, total cadmium and total lead in children's jewellery, total dry weight of leather, the consumer-textile cadmium restriction, dried-sample and non-volatile coating content, and removable sticker or film content), so no content limit can be resolved into a migration cell. The earlier literal-phrase form was over-restrictive in the one direction that mattered: it refused Mexico's identically-based NOM-252 bioavailable rows even when they were named, and because the guard only fires on ids actually named in a cell, a guard-driven exclusion narrowed the strictest-selection pool silently instead of reporting itself. One soluble-basis register row remains outside the guard on phrasing — Minnesota ch. 347 soluble cadmium in children's jewellery, 75 mg/kg (mn_ch347_2010_cd_childrens_jewelry_75ppm) — and it is neither stricter than any value published on this row nor inside the credible-regulator set (US-MN is a state measure carrying its own federal-supersession caveat).

Pb.basis_label: element MIGRATION from scraped-off toy material (EN 71-3 Category III, mg/kg of material) — a migration ceiling, not a total-content ceiling

The Directive's Category III value binds at 23 mg/kg; the ASTM and NOM-252 rows are named so the strictest-selection covers the complete applicable family rather than a subset, and both are looser than the binding value. Total-lead CONTENT law runs in parallel on a different basis and is a companion obligation, not this cell's ceiling: CPSIA s.101 caps total lead at 100 mg/kg in any accessible children's-product substrate (cpsia_pb_childrens_product_substrate_100ppm) and at 90 mg/kg in the dried paint film (cpsia_pb_surface_coating_90ppm); Canada SOR/2016-193 and SOR/2011-17 set 90 mg/kg total lead in surface coating material and in applied stickers and films; Canada SOR/2018-83 sets 90 mg/kg total lead in accessible parts. HMTc requires conformity with both the migration ceiling published here and those content ceilings; the two are different measured quantities and are never combined into one number.

Sn.substantiation: Directive 2009/48/EC Annex II Part III point 13 is the only instrument in the register that sets a numeric tin ceiling for toy material: ASTM F963-17 and ISO 8124-3:2020 do not regulate tin, and NOM-252-SSA1-2011 Table 1 regulates antimony, arsenic, barium, cadmium, total chromium, lead, mercury and selenium and sets no tin limit, so admitting MX to the credible-regulator set does not add a candidate to this cell. The register holds only the Directive's three TOTAL-tin rows. The instrument itself sets TWO tin lines on the same migration basis: total tin (15 000 / 3 750 / 180 000 mg/kg for Categories I / II / III) and organic tin (0.9 / 0.2 / 12 mg/kg), the latter reproduced from the point 13 table on wiki/regulations/eu-2009-48-toy-safety-migration-limits. A prior revision of this cell asserted that the Directive is the only credible sovereign instrument setting a numeric tin ceiling and disclosed only the REACH Annex XVII entry 20 organotin CONTENT restriction; that statement was wrong by omission, because it left the reader unaware that the same instrument caps organic tin at 12 mg/kg for this row's scraped-off (Category III) material while this cell publishes 180 000 mg/kg. The organic-tin migration rows are a recorded REGISTER GAP returned for ingestion through the verified regulatory-fetch pathway; once ingested, this row should gain a published organotin cell beside the total-tin screen, exactly as chromium carries a published Cr(VI) cell beside its total-chromium screen. Organotin is additionally restricted by REACH Annex XVII entry 20 on a total-CONTENT basis (0.1 percent as tin for dibutyltin, and for skin-contact and childcare articles dioctyltin); that is a different measured quantity and is a further companion obligation, not this cell's anchor.

Those organic-tin rows are not in data/evidence/regulatory_limits.csv, so no organotin cell can be compiled and none is invented; the total-tin value is therefore recorded as a screen and the organic-tin ceiling is a BINDING PARALLEL OBLIGATION of equal standing, not an optional companion. NOM-252's stricter 25 mg/kg tier is scoped to preschool school articles, modelling clay and finger paint; none of those material forms is within this row's scope, so that tier is inapplicable here and it binds instead on art-craft-materials and toys-crafts-other, whose scopes name modelling clay, dough and finger paint expressly. TWO PRIOR STATEMENTS ON THIS CELL ARE WITHDRAWN. First, the assertion that ASTM applies a 30 percent analytical correction raising its enforced ceiling to about 86 mg/kg, so that HMTc's use of the nominal 60 mg/kg was over-compliance: that reading is unsubstantiated for the F963 editions relied on, for the reason recorded on the tAs cell, and 60 mg/kg is simply the instrument's figure applied as written. Second, the claim that the ISO 8124-3:2020 modelling-clay and finger-paint chromium limits of 25 mg/kg were a register gap: the same 25 mg/kg value for the same two material forms IS in the register as the Mexican statutory row mx_nom252_2011_cr_total_preschool_clay_fingerpaint_25, and it now binds the rows it applies to. One genuine register gap remains against this cell and is recorded rather than worked around: the EU Cr(III) migration rows of Directive 2009/48/EC point 13 are absent from the register (verified — no Cr-III species exists anywhere in it) and are not invented here. AUDIT ANSWER — NOM-252 PRESCHOOL TIER. The audit scan flags NOM-252-SSA1-2011's stricter chromium tier (25 mg/kg, mx_nom252_2011_cr_total_preschool_clay_fingerpaint_25) as unselected. It is inapplicable to this row for the reason stated above — the tier is scoped to preschool school articles, modelling clay and finger paint, none of which is within this row's scope — and it IS adopted on the three rows whose material forms fall inside it: art-craft-materials, toys-crafts-other and toys-pompoms-fibrous-craft.

Cr(VI) never satisfies the total-chromium cell and the total-chromium screen never satisfies this cell. REACH Annex XVII entry 47 additionally caps Cr(VI) in leather articles at 3 mg/kg on a total-content basis; that content ceiling is a companion obligation for leather components and is not substituted into this migration cell.

toys-stuffing-materials.scope_note: Fill and filling materials used inside stuffed, soft and bean-bag toys: polyester and natural-fibre wadding, foam crumb and slab, plastic granulate and pellets, expanded-polystyrene micro-beads, ground shell, cereal and bean fill, and weighting sand. The row is anchored on EN 71-3 Category I because dry, powder-like and granular fills are squarely within its scope; where the fill is a scraped-off-type material (fibre wadding, foam, discrete pellets) the Directive's Category III values would apply to that component and are looser, so HMTc publishes the stricter Category I ceiling across the whole row. That is a strictest-applicable selection within one instrument, not a blend of two.
toys-stuffing-materials.material: Loose fill: fibre wadding, foam, granulate, pellets, micro-beads, ground shell, cereal/bean fill, weighting sand.
toys-stuffing-materials.components: One test portion per distinct fill material and per distinct colour of dyed fill. Sample the fill as supplied inside the finished toy, not the pre-production lot. Where a toy contains a weighting pouch, the pouch fabric routes to toys-stuffed-bean-bag and the weighting medium is tested here.

toys-stuffing-materials.basis_guard: ^(element migration from [^;]*toy material \(Category (III|I)\)|soluble \(migrated\) element from |bioavailable soluble element from )
toys-stuffing-materials.basis_guard_note: This row's defining material form is dry, powder-like or granular fill, which is EN 71-3 Category I, but its scope also contains scraped-off-type fill (fibre wadding, foam slab, discrete pellets), which is Category III. The guard therefore admits the Directive's Category I AND Category III rows — both are genuinely applicable to material within this row's scope — and both are named on every cell so the strictest binds rather than the category label deciding the number. The guard is kind-based on the extraction quantity rather than a literal-phrase whitelist: it admits any register row whose basis BEGINS with element migration from toy material of an admitted material category, with soluble (migrated) element, or with bioavailable soluble element — the three phrasings the EU, US and Mexican migration instruments use for the same 0.07 M HCl acid-extraction quantity — and it will admit a future sovereign migration row phrased differently again only if that row states the same quantity. Anchored at the start of the basis string, it rejects every total-CONTENT phrasing carried in the register (CPSIA total lead content by weight, lead content in accessible part, RoHS homogeneous material, REACH Annex XVII cadmium and organotin content, total cadmium and total lead in children's jewellery, total dry weight of leather, the consumer-textile cadmium restriction, dried-sample and non-volatile coating content, and removable sticker or film content), so no content limit can be resolved into a migration cell. The earlier literal-phrase form was over-restrictive in the one direction that mattered: it refused Mexico's identically-based NOM-252 bioavailable rows even when they were named, and because the guard only fires on ids actually named in a cell, a guard-driven exclusion narrowed the strictest-selection pool silently instead of reporting itself. One soluble-basis register row remains outside the guard on phrasing — Minnesota ch. 347 soluble cadmium in children's jewellery, 75 mg/kg (mn_ch347_2010_cd_childrens_jewelry_75ppm) — and it is neither stricter than any value published on this row nor inside the credible-regulator set (US-MN is a state measure carrying its own federal-supersession caveat).

Pb.label: Strictest applicable sovereign lead-migration maximum across the material categories this row's scope spans: Directive 2009/48/EC point 13 sets 2.0 mg/kg for Category I (this row's dry, powder-like and granular fill) and 23 mg/kg for Category III (its fibre wadding, foam slab and discrete pellets), against 90 mg/kg under ASTM F963-17 and 90 mg/kg under NOM-252-SSA1-2011. The Category I value binds at 2.0 mg/kg and is published for the whole row.
Pb.substantiation: Both named ids share the migration/soluble basis, so the strictest-selection is basis-clean. Total-lead CONTENT law runs in parallel on a different basis and is a companion obligation, not this cell's ceiling: CPSIA s.101 caps total lead at 100 mg/kg in any accessible children's-product substrate (cpsia_pb_childrens_product_substrate_100ppm) and at 90 mg/kg in the dried paint film (cpsia_pb_surface_coating_90ppm); Canada SOR/2016-193 and SOR/2011-17 set 90 mg/kg total lead in surface coating material and in applied stickers and films; Canada SOR/2018-83 sets 90 mg/kg total lead in accessible parts. HMTc requires conformity with both the migration ceiling published here and those content ceilings; the two are different measured quantities and are never combined into one number. REACH Annex XVII entry 72 as introduced by Regulation (EU) 2018/1513 caps lead, cadmium, arsenic and Cr(VI) at 1 mg/kg in the homogeneous material of consumer clothing and skin-contact textiles. Fill enclosed inside a toy is neither, so entry 72 is not read across as this row's ceiling; where a fibre fill is also supplied as a loose skin-contact textile, entry 72 binds it directly on a total-content basis and is a companion obligation. OVER-COMPLIANCE, DISCLOSED: this row's scope spans two of the Directive's material categories and the stricter of the two is published across the whole row, so for the row's Category III material forms (fibre wadding, foam slab, discrete pellets) the published value is stricter than the Directive's own value for those forms. It is a deliberate protective choice, not those forms' legal ceiling, and the compiled record's candidate set discloses both category values. A previous revision of this config published the Directive's looser Category III figure instead, on the argument that ASTM states its soluble limits in the legacy EN 71-3 / ISO 8124-3 lineage, in which conformity is judged against an analytical-correction-adjusted result, so that ASTM's nominal figure is looser than the Directive's once both are put on a raw-result footing. THAT ARGUMENT IS WITHDRAWN AS UNSUBSTANTIATED. The only repository artifact cited for it, wiki/sources/iso2020-8124-3-toy-migration-elements.md, documents the Table 2 analytical correction for ISO 8124-3:2020 and says of ASTM only that F963 4.3 sits in the same lineage and used the legacy EN 71-3 limits unchanged through F963-07 — a limit-VALUE lineage statement that expressly ends before the F963-08 and later editions this cell relies on, and it attributes no analytical correction to ASTM at all. Sn.label: EU Toy Safety Directive TOTAL-tin migration maximum, strictest across the Category I (15 000 mg/kg, binding) and Category III (180 000 mg/kg) material forms this row's scope spans, recorded as a SCREEN; the same instrument's organic-tin migration ceiling for Category I material, 0.9 mg/kg, is a binding parallel obligation pending register ingestion.
Sn.substantiation: Directive 2009/48/EC Annex II Part III point 13 is the only instrument in the register that sets a numeric tin ceiling for toy material: ASTM F963-17 and ISO 8124-3:2020 do not regulate tin, and NOM-252-SSA1-2011 Table 1 regulates antimony, arsenic, barium, cadmium, total chromium, lead, mercury and selenium and sets no tin limit, so admitting MX to the credible-regulator set does not add a candidate to this cell. The register holds only the Directive's three TOTAL-tin rows. The instrument itself sets TWO tin lines on the same migration basis: total tin (15 000 / 3 750 / 180 000 mg/kg for Categories I / II / III) and organic tin (0.9 / 0.2 / 12 mg/kg), the latter reproduced from the point 13 table on wiki/regulations/eu-2009-48-toy-safety-migration-limits. A prior revision of this cell asserted that the Directive is the only credible sovereign instrument setting a numeric tin ceiling and disclosed only the REACH Annex XVII entry 20 organotin CONTENT restriction; that statement was wrong by omission, because it left the reader unaware that the same instrument caps organic tin at 0.9 mg/kg for this row's dry, powder-like and granular (Category I) material while this cell publishes 15 000 mg/kg. The organic-tin migration rows are a recorded REGISTER GAP returned for ingestion through the verified regulatory-fetch pathway; once ingested, this row should gain a published organotin cell beside the total-tin screen, exactly as chromium carries a published Cr(VI) cell beside its total-chromium screen. Organotin is additionally restricted by REACH Annex XVII entry 20 on a total-CONTENT basis (0.1 percent as tin for dibutyltin, and for skin-contact and childcare articles dioctyltin); that is a different measured quantity and is a further companion obligation, not this cell's anchor. OVER-COMPLIANCE, DISCLOSED: this row's scope spans two of the Directive's material categories and the stricter of the two is published across the whole row, so for the row's Category III material forms (fibre wadding, foam slab, discrete pellets) the published value is stricter than the Directive's own value for those forms. It is a deliberate protective choice, not those forms' legal ceiling, and the compiled record's candidate set discloses both category values. Sn.screen_note: SCREEN, not a protective standalone ceiling. The published figure is TOTAL tin migration: 15 000 mg/kg of material, which is dominated by benign inorganic tin. The health-relevant tin fraction is organotin, and the SAME instrument on the SAME migration basis (Directive 2009/48/EC Annex II Part III point 13) sets a separate organic-tin migration ceiling of 0.9 mg/kg for Category I, 0.2 mg/kg for Category II and 12 mg/kg for Category III — for this row's dry, powder-like and granular (Category I) material that is 0.9 mg/kg, orders of magnitude below the total-tin figure. Those organic-tin rows are not in data/evidence/regulatory_limits.csv, so no organotin cell can be compiled and none is invented; the total-tin value is therefore recorded as a screen and the organic-tin ceiling is a BINDING PARALLEL OBLIGATION of equal standing, not an optional companion. The total-tin result triggers and bounds organotin determination, never substitutes for it.

toys-rattles.name: Rattles

toys-rattles.audit_scope: toy|children'?s (product|article|jewell?ery)|school.?article|student article|surface coating|accessible part|coated with a material
toys-rattles.basis_guard: ^(element migration from [^;]*toy material \(Category (III)\)|soluble \(migrated\) element from |bioavailable soluble element from )
toys-rattles.basis_guard_note: This row's material is tested by scraping (cured coatings, polymers, elastomers, textiles, wood, paper, glass, ceramic and metal), which is EN 71-3 Category III, so the EU alternative in the guard is pinned to Category III alone. The guard is kind-based on the extraction quantity rather than a literal-phrase whitelist: it admits any register row whose basis BEGINS with element migration from toy material of an admitted material category, with soluble (migrated) element, or with bioavailable soluble element — the three phrasings the EU, US and Mexican migration instruments use for the same 0.07 M HCl acid-extraction quantity — and it will admit a future sovereign migration row phrased differently again only if that row states the same quantity. Anchored at the start of the basis string, it rejects every total-CONTENT phrasing carried in the register (CPSIA total lead content by weight, lead content in accessible part, RoHS homogeneous material, REACH Annex XVII cadmium and organotin content, total cadmium and total lead in children's jewellery, total dry weight of leather, the consumer-textile cadmium restriction, dried-sample and non-volatile coating content, and removable sticker or film content), so no content limit can be resolved into a migration cell. The earlier literal-phrase form was over-restrictive in the one direction that mattered: it refused Mexico's identically-based NOM-252 bioavailable rows even when they were named, and because the guard only fires on ids actually named in a cell, a guard-driven exclusion narrowed the strictest-selection pool silently instead of reporting itself. One soluble-basis register row remains outside the guard on phrasing — Minnesota ch. 347 soluble cadmium in children's jewellery, 75 mg/kg (mn_ch347_2010_cd_childrens_jewelry_75ppm) — and it is neither stricter than any value published on this row nor inside the credible-regulator set (US-MN is a state measure carrying its own federal-supersession caveat).
toys-rattles.cross_reference: Teething toys and teethers are HMTc Category 9 (Infant and Child Contact Products), not Category 21. A rattle marketed with a teething surface is certified against both rows.

Pb.basis_label: element MIGRATION from scraped-off toy material (EN 71-3 Category III, mg/kg of material) — a migration ceiling, not a total-content ceiling

The Directive's Category III value binds at 23 mg/kg; the ASTM and NOM-252 rows are named so the strictest-selection covers the complete applicable family rather than a subset, and both are looser than the binding value. Total-lead CONTENT law runs in parallel on a different basis and is a companion obligation, not this cell's ceiling: CPSIA s.101 caps total lead at 100 mg/kg in any accessible children's-product substrate (cpsia_pb_childrens_product_substrate_100ppm) and at 90 mg/kg in the dried paint film (cpsia_pb_surface_coating_90ppm); Canada SOR/2016-193 and SOR/2011-17 set 90 mg/kg total lead in surface coating material and in applied stickers and films; Canada SOR/2018-83 sets 90 mg/kg total lead in accessible parts. HMTc requires conformity with both the migration ceiling published here and those content ceilings; the two are different measured quantities and are never combined into one number.

Ni.label: EU Toy Safety Directive nickel migration maximum for Category III (scraped-off) toy material.
Ni.substantiation: The Toy Safety Directive is the only credible sovereign instrument that sets a numeric nickel ceiling for toy material; ASTM F963-17 and ISO 8124-3:2020 do not regulate nickel at all, and NOM-252-SSA1-2011 Table 1 regulates antimony, arsenic, barium, cadmium, total chromium, lead, mercury and selenium and sets no nickel limit, so admitting MX to the credible-regulator set does not add a candidate to this cell. REACH Annex XVII entry 27 additionally caps nickel RELEASE from articles in prolonged skin contact at 0.5 ug/cm2/week; that is a per-area release rate in a third basis, it is not represented in the register, and it is recorded as a companion obligation and a register gap rather than converted into a mg/kg figure here.

Sn.basis_label: element MIGRATION from scraped-off toy material (EN 71-3 Category III, mg/kg of material) — a migration ceiling, not a total-content ceiling

Sn.substantiation: Directive 2009/48/EC Annex II Part III point 13 is the only instrument in the register that sets a numeric tin ceiling for toy material: ASTM F963-17 and ISO 8124-3:2020 do not regulate tin, and NOM-252-SSA1-2011 Table 1 regulates antimony, arsenic, barium, cadmium, total chromium, lead, mercury and selenium and sets no tin limit, so admitting MX to the credible-regulator set does not add a candidate to this cell. The register holds only the Directive's three TOTAL-tin rows. The instrument itself sets TWO tin lines on the same migration basis: total tin (15 000 / 3 750 / 180 000 mg/kg for Categories I / II / III) and organic tin (0.9 / 0.2 / 12 mg/kg), the latter reproduced from the point 13 table on wiki/regulations/eu-2009-48-toy-safety-migration-limits. A prior revision of this cell asserted that the Directive is the only credible sovereign instrument setting a numeric tin ceiling and disclosed only the REACH Annex XVII entry 20 organotin CONTENT restriction; that statement was wrong by omission, because it left the reader unaware that the same instrument caps organic tin at 12 mg/kg for this row's scraped-off (Category III) material while this cell publishes 180 000 mg/kg. The organic-tin migration rows are a recorded REGISTER GAP returned for ingestion through the verified regulatory-fetch pathway; once ingested, this row should gain a published organotin cell beside the total-tin screen, exactly as chromium carries a published Cr(VI) cell beside its total-chromium screen. Organotin is additionally restricted by REACH Annex XVII entry 20 on a total-CONTENT basis (0.1 percent as tin for dibutyltin, and for skin-contact and childcare articles dioctyltin); that is a different measured quantity and is a further companion obligation, not this cell's anchor.
Sn.screen_note: SCREEN, not a protective standalone ceiling. The published figure is TOTAL tin migration: 180 000 mg/kg of material, which is dominated by benign inorganic tin. The health-relevant tin fraction is organotin, and the SAME instrument on the SAME migration basis (Directive 2009/48/EC Annex II Part III point 13) sets a separate organic-tin migration ceiling of 0.9 mg/kg for Category I, 0.2 mg/kg for Category II and 12 mg/kg for Category III — for this row's scraped-off (Category III) material that is 12 mg/kg, orders of magnitude below the total-tin figure. Those organic-tin rows are not in data/evidence/regulatory_limits.csv, so no organotin cell can be compiled and none is invented; the total-tin value is therefore recorded as a screen and the organic-tin ceiling is a BINDING PARALLEL OBLIGATION of equal standing, not an optional companion. The total-tin result triggers and bounds organotin determination, never substitutes for it.

toys-squeeze.audit_scope: toy|children'?s (product|article|jewell?ery)|school.?article|student article|surface coating|accessible part|coated with a material
toys-squeeze.basis_guard: ^(element migration from [^;]*toy material \(Category (III)\)|soluble \(migrated\) element from |bioavailable soluble element from )
toys-squeeze.basis_guard_note: This row's material is tested by scraping (cured coatings, polymers, elastomers, textiles, wood, paper, glass, ceramic and metal), which is EN 71-3 Category III, so the EU alternative in the guard is pinned to Category III alone. The guard is kind-based on the extraction quantity rather than a literal-phrase whitelist: it admits any register row whose basis BEGINS with element migration from toy material of an admitted material category, with soluble (migrated) element, or with bioavailable soluble element — the three phrasings the EU, US and Mexican migration instruments use for the same 0.07 M HCl acid-extraction quantity — and it will admit a future sovereign migration row phrased differently again only if that row states the same quantity. Anchored at the start of the basis string, it rejects every total-CONTENT phrasing carried in the register (CPSIA total lead content by weight, lead content in accessible part, RoHS homogeneous material, REACH Annex XVII cadmium and organotin content, total cadmium and total lead in children's jewellery, total dry weight of leather, the consumer-textile cadmium restriction, dried-sample and non-volatile coating content, and removable sticker or film content), so no content limit can be resolved into a migration cell. The earlier literal-phrase form was over-restrictive in the one direction that mattered: it refused Mexico's identically-based NOM-252 bioavailable rows even when they were named, and because the guard only fires on ids actually named in a cell, a guard-driven exclusion narrowed the strictest-selection pool silently instead of reporting itself. One soluble-basis register row remains outside the guard on phrasing — Minnesota ch. 347 soluble cadmium in children's jewellery, 75 mg/kg (mn_ch347_2010_cd_childrens_jewelry_75ppm) — and it is neither stricter than any value published on this row nor inside the credible-regulator set (US-MN is a state measure carrying its own federal-supersession caveat).

Pb.basis_label: element MIGRATION from scraped-off toy material (EN 71-3 Category III, mg/kg of material) — a migration ceiling, not a total-content ceiling

Pb.substantiation: All named ids state one measured quantity — the acid-soluble element that migrates from accessible toy material under the EN 71-3 / ISO 8124-3 0.07 M HCl 37 C extraction, which NOM-252-SSA1-2011 calls bioavailable soluble element — so the strictest-selection is basis-clean. Total-lead CONTENT law runs in parallel on a different basis and is a companion obligation, not this cell's ceiling: CPSIA s.101 caps total lead at 100 mg/kg in any accessible children's-product substrate (cpsia_pb_childrens_product_substrate_100ppm) and at 90 mg/kg in the dried paint film (cpsia_pb_surface_coating_90ppm); Canada SOR/2016-193 and SOR/2011-17 set 90 mg/kg total lead in surface coating material and in applied stickers and films; Canada SOR/2018-83 sets 90 mg/kg total lead in accessible parts. HMTc requires conformity with both the migration ceiling published here and those content ceilings; the two are different measured quantities and are never combined into one number.

tAs.basis_label: acid-soluble / MIGRATED element from accessible toy material (EN 71-3 / ISO 8124-3 0.07 M HCl, 37 C, mg/kg of material). tAs.label: Strictest applicable sovereign total-arsenic migration maximum for Category III (scraped-off) toy material, taken across the whole migration family: ASTM F963-17 4.3.5 soluble arsenic 25 mg/kg (mandatory in the US under CPSIA s.106 / 16 CFR 1250) and NOM-252-SSA1-2011 Table 1 bioavailable arsenic 25 mg/kg (MX) both bind at 25 mg/kg, below the Directive's point 13 Category III value of 47 mg/kg.

A previous revision of this config published the Directive's looser Category III figure instead, on the argument that ASTM states its soluble limits in the legacy EN 71-3 / ISO 8124-3 lineage, in which conformity is judged against an analytical-correction-adjusted result, so that ASTM's nominal figure is looser than the Directive's once both are put on a raw-result footing. THAT ARGUMENT IS WITHDRAWN AS UNSUBSTANTIATED. The only repository artifact cited for it, wiki/sources/iso2020-8124-3-toy-migration-elements.md, documents the Table 2 analytical correction for ISO 8124-3:2020 and says of ASTM only that F963 4.3 sits in the same lineage and used the legacy EN 71-3 limits unchanged through F963-07 — a limit-VALUE lineage statement that expressly ends before the F963-08 and later editions this cell relies on, and it attributes no analytical correction to ASTM at all. Ni.label: EU Toy Safety Directive nickel migration maximum for Category III (scraped-off) toy material.
Ni.substantiation: The Toy Safety Directive is the only credible sovereign instrument that sets a numeric nickel ceiling for toy material; ASTM F963-17 and ISO 8124-3:2020 do not regulate nickel at all, and NOM-252-SSA1-2011 Table 1 regulates antimony, arsenic, barium, cadmium, total chromium, lead, mercury and selenium and sets no nickel limit, so admitting MX to the credible-regulator set does not add a candidate to this cell. Sn.basis_label: element MIGRATION from scraped-off toy material (EN 71-3 Category III, mg/kg of material) — a migration ceiling, not a total-content ceiling

Sn.substantiation: Directive 2009/48/EC Annex II Part III point 13 is the only instrument in the register that sets a numeric tin ceiling for toy material: ASTM F963-17 and ISO 8124-3:2020 do not regulate tin, and NOM-252-SSA1-2011 Table 1 regulates antimony, arsenic, barium, cadmium, total chromium, lead, mercury and selenium and sets no tin limit, so admitting MX to the credible-regulator set does not add a candidate to this cell. The register holds only the Directive's three TOTAL-tin rows. The instrument itself sets TWO tin lines on the same migration basis: total tin (15 000 / 3 750 / 180 000 mg/kg for Categories I / II / III) and organic tin (0.9 / 0.2 / 12 mg/kg), the latter reproduced from the point 13 table on wiki/regulations/eu-2009-48-toy-safety-migration-limits. A prior revision of this cell asserted that the Directive is the only credible sovereign instrument setting a numeric tin ceiling and disclosed only the REACH Annex XVII entry 20 organotin CONTENT restriction; that statement was wrong by omission, because it left the reader unaware that the same instrument caps organic tin at 12 mg/kg for this row's scraped-off (Category III) material while this cell publishes 180 000 mg/kg. The organic-tin migration rows are a recorded REGISTER GAP returned for ingestion through the verified regulatory-fetch pathway; once ingested, this row should gain a published organotin cell beside the total-tin screen, exactly as chromium carries a published Cr(VI) cell beside its total-chromium screen. Organotin is additionally restricted by REACH Annex XVII entry 20 on a total-CONTENT basis (0.1 percent as tin for dibutyltin, and for skin-contact and childcare articles dioctyltin); that is a different measured quantity and is a further companion obligation, not this cell's anchor.
Sn.screen_note: SCREEN, not a protective standalone ceiling. The published figure is TOTAL tin migration: 180 000 mg/kg of material, which is dominated by benign inorganic tin. The health-relevant tin fraction is organotin, and the SAME instrument on the SAME migration basis (Directive 2009/48/EC Annex II Part III point 13) sets a separate organic-tin migration ceiling of 0.9 mg/kg for Category I, 0.2 mg/kg for Category II and 12 mg/kg for Category III — for this row's scraped-off (Category III) material that is 12 mg/kg, orders of magnitude below the total-tin figure. Those organic-tin rows are not in data/evidence/regulatory_limits.csv, so no organotin cell can be compiled and none is invented; the total-tin value is therefore recorded as a screen and the organic-tin ceiling is a BINDING PARALLEL OBLIGATION of equal standing, not an optional companion. The total-tin result triggers and bounds organotin determination, never substitutes for it.
