Ni.basis_label: element MIGRATION from scraped-off toy material (EN 71-3 Category III, mg/kg of material) — a migration ceiling, not a total-content ceiling
Ni.label: EU Toy Safety Directive nickel migration maximum for Category III (scraped-off) toy material.
Ni.substantiation: The Toy Safety Directive is the only credible sovereign instrument that sets a numeric nickel ceiling for toy material; ASTM F963-17 and ISO 8124-3:2020 do not regulate nickel at all, and NOM-252-SSA1-2011 Table 1 regulates antimony, arsenic, barium, cadmium, total chromium, lead, mercury and selenium and sets no nickel limit, so admitting MX to the credible-regulator set does not add a candidate to this cell. The Directive's nickel figures are permissive relative to the other panel analytes and HMTc publishes them as written rather than substituting an occurrence-derived or invented value. REACH Annex XVII entry 27 additionally caps nickel RELEASE from articles in prolonged skin contact at 0.5 ug/cm2/week; that is a per-area release rate in a third basis, it is not represented in the register, and it is recorded as a companion obligation and a register gap rather than converted into a mg/kg figure here. Nickel is the principal material risk on this row because sintered neodymium magnets are conventionally nickel-plated and a defeated encapsulation exposes bare plating. The Toy Safety Directive's nickel migration ceiling is nonetheless the only sovereign number available in this basis, and HMTc publishes it as written. The REACH Annex XVII entry 27 nickel-release limit for prolonged skin contact (0.5 ug/cm2/week) is the tighter parallel control for exposed plated parts; it is a per-area release rate, is absent from the register, and is recorded as a companion obligation and a register gap.

Sn.basis_label: element MIGRATION from scraped-off toy material (EN 71-3 Category III, mg/kg of material) — a migration ceiling, not a total-content ceiling
Sn.label: EU Toy Safety Directive TOTAL-tin migration maximum for Category III (scraped-off) toy material, recorded as a SCREEN; the same instrument's organic-tin migration ceiling for Category III material, 12 mg/kg, is a binding parallel obligation pending register ingestion.
Sn.substantiation: Directive 2009/48/EC Annex II Part III point 13 is the only instrument in the register that sets a numeric tin ceiling for toy material: ASTM F963-17 and ISO 8124-3:2020 do not regulate tin, and NOM-252-SSA1-2011 Table 1 regulates antimony, arsenic, barium, cadmium, total chromium, lead, mercury and selenium and sets no tin limit, so admitting MX to the credible-regulator set does not add a candidate to this cell. The register holds only the Directive's three TOTAL-tin rows. The instrument itself sets TWO tin lines on the same migration basis: total tin (15 000 / 3 750 / 180 000 mg/kg for Categories I / II / III) and organic tin (0.9 / 0.2 / 12 mg/kg), the latter reproduced from the point 13 table on wiki/regulations/eu-2009-48-toy-safety-migration-limits. A prior revision of this cell asserted that the Directive is the only credible sovereign instrument setting a numeric tin ceiling and disclosed only the REACH Annex XVII entry 20 organotin CONTENT restriction; that statement was wrong by omission, because it left the reader unaware that the same instrument caps organic tin at 12 mg/kg for this row's scraped-off (Category III) material while this cell publishes 180 000 mg/kg. The organic-tin migration rows are a recorded REGISTER GAP returned for ingestion through the verified regulatory-fetch pathway; once ingested, this row should gain a published organotin cell beside the total-tin screen, exactly as chromium carries a published Cr(VI) cell beside its total-chromium screen. Organotin is additionally restricted by REACH Annex XVII entry 20 on a total-CONTENT basis (0.1 percent as tin for dibutyltin, and for skin-contact and childcare articles dioctyltin); that is a different measured quantity and is a further companion obligation, not this cell's anchor.
Sn.screen_note: SCREEN, not a protective standalone ceiling. The published figure is TOTAL tin migration: 180 000 mg/kg of material, which is dominated by benign inorganic tin. The health-relevant tin fraction is organotin, and the SAME instrument on the SAME migration basis (Directive 2009/48/EC Annex II Part III point 13) sets a separate organic-tin migration ceiling of 0.9 mg/kg for Category I, 0.2 mg/kg for Category II and 12 mg/kg for Category III — for this row's scraped-off (Category III) material that is 12 mg/kg, orders of magnitude below the total-tin figure. Those organic-tin rows are not in data/evidence/regulatory_limits.csv, so no organotin cell can be compiled and none is invented; the total-tin value is therefore recorded as a screen and the organic-tin ceiling is a BINDING PARALLEL OBLIGATION of equal standing, not an optional companion. The total-tin result triggers and bounds organotin determination, never substitutes for it.

The 2019/1922 amendment already tightened these values by roughly 2.5x; HMTc publishes the amended figures as written.

A migration ceiling, not a total-content ceiling.
Cr.screen_note: SCREEN, not a protective standalone ceiling. Total chromium in toy material is dominated by benign Cr(III) from pigments, stainless components and tanned leather; the health-relevant species is Cr(VI), which carries its own published cell on this row. The total-chromium result is used to trigger and to bound Cr(VI) speciation, never as a substitute for it.
Cr.label: Total-chromium migration maximum taken over the two credible sovereign instruments that set one on this basis: ASTM F963-17 4.3.5 soluble total chromium 60 mg/kg (mandatory in the US under CPSIA s.106) and NOM-252-SSA1-2011 Table 1 bioavailable total chromium 60 mg/kg for toy or school-article material other than modelling clay and finger paint (MX). Both agree at 60 mg/kg. Recorded as a SCREEN, not a protective standalone ceiling.
Cr.substantiation: The EU Toy Safety Directive splits chromium into Cr(III) and Cr(VI) and sets no TOTAL-chromium ceiling, so the total-chromium value is taken over the two credible sovereign instruments that do set one on the acid-soluble migration basis. ASTM F963-17 and NOM-252-SSA1-2011 agree at 60 mg/kg and HMTc applies that figure to the laboratory's analytical result as reported. NOM-252's stricter 25 mg/kg tier is scoped to preschool school articles, modelling clay and finger paint; none of those material forms is within this row's scope, so that tier is inapplicable here and it binds instead on art-craft-materials and toys-crafts-other, whose scopes name modelling clay, dough and finger paint expressly. TWO PRIOR STATEMENTS ON THIS CELL ARE WITHDRAWN. First, the assertion that ASTM applies a 30 percent analytical correction raising its enforced ceiling to about 86 mg/kg, so that HMTc's use of the nominal 60 mg/kg was over-compliance: that reading is unsubstantiated for the F963 editions relied on, for the reason recorded on the tAs cell, and 60 mg/kg is simply the instrument's figure applied as written. Second, the claim that the ISO 8124-3:2020 modelling-clay and finger-paint chromium limits of 25 mg/kg were a register gap: the same 25 mg/kg value for the same two material forms IS in the register as the Mexican statutory row mx_nom252_2011_cr_total_preschool_clay_fingerpaint_25, and it now binds the rows it applies to. One genuine register gap remains against this cell and is recorded rather than worked around: the EU Cr(III) migration rows of Directive 2009/48/EC point 13 are absent from the register (verified — no Cr-III species exists anywhere in it) and are not invented here. AUDIT ANSWER — NOM-252 PRESCHOOL TIER. The audit scan flags NOM-252-SSA1-2011's stricter chromium tier (25 mg/kg, mx_nom252_2011_cr_total_preschool_clay_fingerpaint_25) as unselected. It is inapplicable to this row for the reason stated above — the tier is scoped to preschool school articles, modelling clay and finger paint, none of which is within this row's scope — and it IS adopted on the three rows whose material forms fall inside it: art-craft-materials, toys-crafts-other and toys-pompoms-fibrous-craft.

Cr-VI.basis_label: element MIGRATION from scraped-off toy material (EN 71-3 Category III, mg/kg of material) — a migration ceiling, not a total-content ceiling
Cr-VI.label: EU Toy Safety Directive hexavalent-chromium migration maximum for Category III (scraped-off) toy material.
Cr-VI.substantiation: The Toy Safety Directive is the only credible sovereign instrument setting a Cr(VI)-specific ceiling for toy material (ASTM F963-17, ISO 8124-3:2020 and NOM-252-SSA1-2011 all regulate TOTAL chromium only, so admitting MX to the credible-regulator set does not add a candidate to this cell; NOM-252's total-chromium rows are named on the Cr cell, never here). Cr(VI) never satisfies the total-chromium cell and the total-chromium screen never satisfies this cell. REACH Annex XVII entry 47 additionally caps Cr(VI) in leather articles at 3 mg/kg on a total-content basis; that content ceiling is a companion obligation for leather components and is not substituted into this migration cell.

toys-projectile-guns.name: Projectile toys and toy guns

toys-projectile-guns.scope_note: Projectile-firing toys and toy firearms: dart and disc launchers, bow-and-arrow sets, catapults, water guns and cap-firing toys, together with their projectiles. Projectiles are frequently mouthed and are always sampled as separate components. Kinetic-energy and protective-tip requirements under EN 71-1 and ASTM F963-17 are mechanical requirements and are not converted into a metals number.
toys-projectile-guns.material: Launcher housing polymer and metal; spring; foam or elastomer dart; suction cup; printed decoration.
toys-projectile-guns.components: Separate test portions for launcher housing (per colour), metal spring or barrel, foam dart body, elastomer or suction-cup tip, printed decoration, and any tethered projectile cord. Cap-firing toys route their percussion caps to toys-crafts-other.
toys-projectile-guns.audit_scope: toy|children'?s (product|article|jewell?ery)|school.?article|student article|surface coating|accessible part|coated with a material
toys-projectile-guns.basis_guard: ^(element migration from [^;]*toy material \(Category (III)\)|soluble \(migrated\) element from |bioavailable soluble element from )
toys-projectile-guns.basis_guard_note: This row's material is tested by scraping (cured coatings, polymers, elastomers, textiles, wood, paper, glass, ceramic and metal), which is EN 71-3 Category III, so the EU alternative in the guard is pinned to Category III alone. The guard is kind-based on the extraction quantity rather than a literal-phrase whitelist: it admits any register row whose basis BEGINS with element migration from toy material of an admitted material category, with soluble (migrated) element, or with bioavailable soluble element — the three phrasings the EU, US and Mexican migration instruments use for the same 0.07 M HCl acid-extraction quantity — and it will admit a future sovereign migration row phrased differently again only if that row states the same quantity. Anchored at the start of the basis string, it rejects every total-CONTENT phrasing carried in the register (CPSIA total lead content by weight, lead content in accessible part, RoHS homogeneous material, REACH Annex XVII cadmium and organotin content, total cadmium and total lead in children's jewellery, total dry weight of leather, the consumer-textile cadmium restriction, dried-sample and non-volatile coating content, and removable sticker or film content), so no content limit can be resolved into a migration cell. The earlier literal-phrase form was over-restrictive in the one direction that mattered: it refused Mexico's identically-based NOM-252 bioavailable rows even when they were named, and because the guard only fires on ids actually named in a cell, a guard-driven exclusion narrowed the strictest-selection pool silently instead of reporting itself. One soluble-basis register row remains outside the guard on phrasing — Minnesota ch. 347 soluble cadmium in children's jewellery, 75 mg/kg (mn_ch347_2010_cd_childrens_jewelry_75ppm) — and it is neither stricter than any value published on this row nor inside the credible-regulator set (US-MN is a state measure carrying its own federal-supersession caveat).

Pb.basis_label: element MIGRATION from scraped-off toy material (EN 71-3 Category III, mg/kg of material) — a migration ceiling, not a total-content ceiling
Pb.label: Strictest applicable sovereign lead-migration maximum for Category III (scraped-off) toy material, taken across the whole migration family: Directive 2009/48/EC point 13 Category III 23 mg/kg (binding), ASTM F963-17 4.3.5 soluble lead 90 mg/kg (mandatory in the US under CPSIA s.106), and NOM-252-SSA1-2011 Table 1 bioavailable lead 90 mg/kg (MX).
Pb.substantiation: All named ids state one measured quantity — the acid-soluble element that migrates from accessible toy material under the EN 71-3 / ISO 8124-3 0.07 M HCl 37 C extraction, which NOM-252-SSA1-2011 calls bioavailable soluble element — so the strictest-selection is basis-clean. The Directive's Category III value binds at 23 mg/kg; the ASTM and NOM-252 rows are named so the strictest-selection covers the complete applicable family rather than a subset, and both are looser than the binding value. Total-lead CONTENT law runs in parallel on a different basis and is a companion obligation, not this cell's ceiling: CPSIA s.101 caps total lead at 100 mg/kg in any accessible children's-product substrate (cpsia_pb_childrens_product_substrate_100ppm) and at 90 mg/kg in the dried paint film (cpsia_pb_surface_coating_90ppm); Canada SOR/2016-193 and SOR/2011-17 set 90 mg/kg total lead in surface coating material and in applied stickers and films; Canada SOR/2018-83 sets 90 mg/kg total lead in accessible parts. HMTc requires conformity with both the migration ceiling published here and those content ceilings; the two are different measured quantities and are never combined into one number.

Those are content ceilings on a different measured quantity and are far more permissive than the migration ceiling published here; they are recorded as companion obligations and are deliberately NOT used to set this cell, because publishing a 0.1-percent paint-content figure as the HMTc cadmium ceiling would replace a protective migration limit with a permissive content limit.

not_material.regulatory_basis: Directive 2009/48/EC Annex II Part III point 13 (arsenic, total element, three material categories); ASTM F963-17 4.3.5 soluble arsenic (total element), mandatory in the US under CPSIA s.106; ISO 8124-3:2020 Table 1 (arsenic, total element). NOM-252-SSA1-2011 Table 1 (arsenic, total element, both scope tiers), mandatory in Mexico since 2012-08-13. None of the four speciates arsenic.
not_material.jurisdictions_checked: EU (2009/48/EC as amended), UK (retained TSD / Toys (Safety) Regulations 2011), US (CPSIA s.106 / 16 CFR 1250 / ASTM F963-17), CA (SOR/2011-17, SOR/2016-193, SOR/2018-83), AU-NZ, CODEX, MX (NOM-252-SSA1-2011), international (ISO 8124-3:2020)

tHg.basis_label: acid-soluble / MIGRATED element from accessible toy material (EN 71-3 / ISO 8124-3 0.07 M HCl, 37 C, mg/kg of material). The three instruments in this family state the same measured quantity in three phrasings: Directive 2009/48/EC point 13 element migration, which IS split by material category and whose applicable member here is the Category III (scraped-off material) value; ASTM F963-17 4.3.5 soluble (migrated) element; and NOM-252-SSA1-2011 bioavailable soluble element. The ASTM and NOM-252 limits are not EN 71-3 material-category scoped, so where one of them binds, the published ceiling carries no material-category qualifier. A migration ceiling, not a total-content ceiling.
tHg.label: Strictest applicable sovereign total-mercury migration maximum for Category III (scraped-off) toy material, taken across the whole migration family: ASTM F963-17 4.3.5 soluble mercury 60 mg/kg (mandatory in the US under CPSIA s.106 / 16 CFR 1250) and NOM-252-SSA1-2011 Table 1 bioavailable mercury 60 mg/kg (MX) both bind at 60 mg/kg, below the Directive's point 13 Category III value of 94 mg/kg.
tHg.substantiation: All named ids state one measured quantity — the acid-soluble element that migrates from accessible toy material under the EN 71-3 / ISO 8124-3 0.07 M HCl 37 C extraction, which NOM-252-SSA1-2011 calls bioavailable soluble element — so the strictest-selection is basis-clean. Two of the three instruments set 60 mg/kg against the Directive's 94 mg/kg, so 60 mg/kg is the published ceiling and HMTc applies it to the laboratory's analytical result as reported. A previous revision of this config published the Directive's looser Category III figure instead, on the argument that ASTM states its soluble limits in the legacy EN 71-3 / ISO 8124-3 lineage, in which conformity is judged against an analytical-correction-adjusted result, so that ASTM's nominal figure is looser than the Directive's once both are put on a raw-result footing. THAT ARGUMENT IS WITHDRAWN AS UNSUBSTANTIATED. The only repository artifact cited for it, wiki/sources/iso2020-8124-3-toy-migration-elements.md, documents the Table 2 analytical correction for ISO 8124-3:2020 and says of ASTM only that F963 4.3 sits in the same lineage and used the legacy EN 71-3 limits unchanged through F963-07 — a limit-VALUE lineage statement that expressly ends before the F963-08 and later editions this cell relies on, and it attributes no analytical correction to ASTM at all. The register row's own notes record only that the values are unchanged across F963-08/-11/-16/-17/-23. HMTc does not publish a ceiling above a figure made mandatory by CPSIA s.106 / 16 CFR 1250 on an unsubstantiated reading of a conformity clause. If ASTM F963-17 4.3.5 / 8.3 is later ingested as a source page that quotes the conformity-decision rule and it does specify a correction, the question may be reopened on that record; until then the stricter figure binds, which is also the position already published on wiki/regulations/astm-f963-soluble-migration and wiki/regulations/eu-2009-48-toy-safety-migration-limits. Separately, Canada SOR/2016-193 and SOR/2011-17 set 10 mg/kg TOTAL mercury in surface coating material and in applied stickers and films. That is a total-content ceiling on the coating, a different measured quantity from migration, and it is stricter than the migration ceiling published here. It is carried as a companion obligation rather than substituted into this cell, and HMTc requires conformity with BOTH: an article whose coating carries more than 10 mg/kg total mercury does not certify, whatever its migration result. AUDIT ANSWER — NOM-252 PRESCHOOL TIER. The audit scan flags NOM-252-SSA1-2011's stricter mercury tier (25 mg/kg, mx_nom252_2011_thg_preschool_clay_fingerpaint_25) as unselected. It is inapplicable to this row: that tier is scoped to preschool SCHOOL ARTICLES, modelling clay and finger paint, and NOM-252's general tier expressly covers any toy or school-article material EXCEPT modelling clay and finger paint, so a toy of this row's description sits in the general tier at 60 mg/kg. The stricter tier is adopted where the row's material genuinely is a school-craft, modelling-clay or finger-paint form: it binds on art-craft-materials, toys-crafts-other and toys-pompoms-fibrous-craft.

not_material.rationale: Methylmercury is produced by microbial methylation in aquatic systems and reaches humans by diet. a launcher body, projectile, dart tip or suction cup carries no methylation pathway and no dietary route, and no sovereign toy instrument sets a methylmercury limit: every toy mercury limit (2009/48/EC point 13, ASTM F963-17 4.3.5, ISO 8124-3:2020, NOM-252-SSA1-2011, Canada SOR/2011-17 and SOR/2016-193) is on total mercury. Any organomercury fraction is bounded by the published total-mercury migration ceiling by identity (MeHg <= tHg).
not_material.reference_method: Total-mercury migration on this row's EN 71-3 material category (0.07 M HCl, 37 C, CV-AAS or ICP-MS). Methylmercury speciation is run only on reflex, whenever total-mercury migration exceeds 50 percent of the published ceiling.
not_material.regulatory_basis: Directive 2009/48/EC Annex II Part III point 13 (mercury, total element); ASTM F963-17 4.3.5 soluble mercury (total element); ISO 8124-3:2020 Table 1 (mercury, total element); Canada SOR/2011-17 and SOR/2016-193 (total mercury in surface coating material). NOM-252-SSA1-2011 Table 1 (mercury, total element, both scope tiers). None speciates mercury.

Ni.basis_label: element MIGRATION from scraped-off toy material (EN 71-3 Category III, mg/kg of material) — a migration ceiling, not a total-content ceiling
Ni.label: EU Toy Safety Directive nickel migration maximum for Category III (scraped-off) toy material.
Ni.substantiation: The Toy Safety Directive is the only credible sovereign instrument that sets a numeric nickel ceiling for toy material; ASTM F963-17 and ISO 8124-3:2020 do not regulate nickel at all, and NOM-252-SSA1-2011 Table 1 regulates antimony, arsenic, barium, cadmium, total chromium, lead, mercury and selenium and sets no nickel limit, so admitting MX to the credible-regulator set does not add a candidate to this cell. The Directive's nickel figures are permissive relative to the other panel analytes and HMTc publishes them as written rather than substituting an occurrence-derived or invented value. REACH Annex XVII entry 27 additionally caps nickel RELEASE from articles in prolonged skin contact at 0.5 ug/cm2/week; that is a per-area release rate in a third basis, it is not represented in the register, and it is recorded as a companion obligation and a register gap rather than converted into a mg/kg figure here.

Sn.basis_label: element MIGRATION from scraped-off toy material (EN 71-3 Category III, mg/kg of material) — a migration ceiling, not a total-content ceiling
Sn.label: EU Toy Safety Directive TOTAL-tin migration maximum for Category III (scraped-off) toy material, recorded as a SCREEN; the same instrument's organic-tin migration ceiling for Category III material, 12 mg/kg, is a binding parallel obligation pending register ingestion.
Sn.substantiation: Directive 2009/48/EC Annex II Part III point 13 is the only instrument in the register that sets a numeric tin ceiling for toy material: ASTM F963-17 and ISO 8124-3:2020 do not regulate tin, and NOM-252-SSA1-2011 Table 1 regulates antimony, arsenic, barium, cadmium, total chromium, lead, mercury and selenium and sets no tin limit, so admitting MX to the credible-regulator set does not add a candidate to this cell. The register holds only the Directive's three TOTAL-tin rows. The instrument itself sets TWO tin lines on the same migration basis: total tin (15 000 / 3 750 / 180 000 mg/kg for Categories I / II / III) and organic tin (0.9 / 0.2 / 12 mg/kg), the latter reproduced from the point 13 table on wiki/regulations/eu-2009-48-toy-safety-migration-limits. A prior revision of this cell asserted that the Directive is the only credible sovereign instrument setting a numeric tin ceiling and disclosed only the REACH Annex XVII entry 20 organotin CONTENT restriction; that statement was wrong by omission, because it left the reader unaware that the same instrument caps organic tin at 12 mg/kg for this row's scraped-off (Category III) material while this cell publishes 180 000 mg/kg. The organic-tin migration rows are a recorded REGISTER GAP returned for ingestion through the verified regulatory-fetch pathway; once ingested, this row should gain a published organotin cell beside the total-tin screen, exactly as chromium carries a published Cr(VI) cell beside its total-chromium screen. Organotin is additionally restricted by REACH Annex XVII entry 20 on a total-CONTENT basis (0.1 percent as tin for dibutyltin, and for skin-contact and childcare articles dioctyltin); that is a different measured quantity and is a further companion obligation, not this cell's anchor.
Sn.screen_note: SCREEN, not a protective standalone ceiling. The published figure is TOTAL tin migration: 180 000 mg/kg of material, which is dominated by benign inorganic tin. The health-relevant tin fraction is organotin, and the SAME instrument on the SAME migration basis (Directive 2009/48/EC Annex II Part III point 13) sets a separate organic-tin migration ceiling of 0.9 mg/kg for Category I, 0.2 mg/kg for Category II and 12 mg/kg for Category III — for this row's scraped-off (Category III) material that is 12 mg/kg, orders of magnitude below the total-tin figure. Those organic-tin rows are not in data/evidence/regulatory_limits.csv, so no organotin cell can be compiled and none is invented; the total-tin value is therefore recorded as a screen and the organic-tin ceiling is a BINDING PARALLEL OBLIGATION of equal standing, not an optional companion. The total-tin result triggers and bounds organotin determination, never substitutes for it.

Al.basis_label: element MIGRATION from scraped-off toy material (EN 71-3 Category III, mg/kg of material) — a migration ceiling, not a total-content ceiling
Al.label: EU Toy Safety Directive aluminium migration maximum for Category III (scraped-off) toy material (as amended by Directive (EU) 2019/1922).
Al.substantiation: The Toy Safety Directive is the only credible sovereign instrument setting a numeric aluminium ceiling for toy material; ASTM F963-17 and ISO 8124-3:2020 do not regulate aluminium, and NOM-252-SSA1-2011 Table 1 regulates antimony, arsenic, barium, cadmium, total chromium, lead, mercury and selenium and sets no aluminium limit, so admitting MX to the credible-regulator set does not add a candidate to this cell. The 2019/1922 amendment already tightened these values by roughly 2.5x; HMTc publishes the amended figures as written.

The three instruments in this family state the same measured quantity in three phrasings: Directive 2009/48/EC point 13 element migration, which IS split by material category and whose applicable member here is the Category III (scraped-off material) value; ASTM F963-17 4.3.5 soluble (migrated) element; and NOM-252-SSA1-2011 bioavailable soluble element. The ASTM and NOM-252 limits are not EN 71-3 material-category scoped, so where one of them binds, the published ceiling carries no material-category qualifier. A migration ceiling, not a total-content ceiling.
Cr.screen_note: SCREEN, not a protective standalone ceiling. Total chromium in toy material is dominated by benign Cr(III) from pigments, stainless components and tanned leather; the health-relevant species is Cr(VI), which carries its own published cell on this row. The total-chromium result is used to trigger and to bound Cr(VI) speciation, never as a substitute for it.
Cr.label: Total-chromium migration maximum taken over the two credible sovereign instruments that set one on this basis: ASTM F963-17 4.3.5 soluble total chromium 60 mg/kg (mandatory in the US under CPSIA s.106) and NOM-252-SSA1-2011 Table 1 bioavailable total chromium 60 mg/kg for toy or school-article material other than modelling clay and finger paint (MX). Both agree at 60 mg/kg. Recorded as a SCREEN, not a protective standalone ceiling.
Cr.substantiation: The EU Toy Safety Directive splits chromium into Cr(III) and Cr(VI) and sets no TOTAL-chromium ceiling, so the total-chromium value is taken over the two credible sovereign instruments that do set one on the acid-soluble migration basis. ASTM F963-17 and NOM-252-SSA1-2011 agree at 60 mg/kg and HMTc applies that figure to the laboratory's analytical result as reported. NOM-252's stricter 25 mg/kg tier is scoped to preschool school articles, modelling clay and finger paint; none of those material forms is within this row's scope, so that tier is inapplicable here and it binds instead on art-craft-materials and toys-crafts-other, whose scopes name modelling clay, dough and finger paint expressly. TWO PRIOR STATEMENTS ON THIS CELL ARE WITHDRAWN. First, the assertion that ASTM applies a 30 percent analytical correction raising its enforced ceiling to about 86 mg/kg, so that HMTc's use of the nominal 60 mg/kg was over-compliance: that reading is unsubstantiated for the F963 editions relied on, for the reason recorded on the tAs cell, and 60 mg/kg is simply the instrument's figure applied as written. Second, the claim that the ISO 8124-3:2020 modelling-clay and finger-paint chromium limits of 25 mg/kg were a register gap: the same 25 mg/kg value for the same two material forms IS in the register as the Mexican statutory row mx_nom252_2011_cr_total_preschool_clay_fingerpaint_25, and it now binds the rows it applies to. One genuine register gap remains against this cell and is recorded rather than worked around: the EU Cr(III) migration rows of Directive 2009/48/EC point 13 are absent from the register (verified — no Cr-III species exists anywhere in it) and are not invented here. AUDIT ANSWER — NOM-252 PRESCHOOL TIER. The audit scan flags NOM-252-SSA1-2011's stricter chromium tier (25 mg/kg, mx_nom252_2011_cr_total_preschool_clay_fingerpaint_25) as unselected. It is inapplicable to this row for the reason stated above — the tier is scoped to preschool school articles, modelling clay and finger paint, none of which is within this row's scope — and it IS adopted on the three rows whose material forms fall inside it: art-craft-materials, toys-crafts-other and toys-pompoms-fibrous-craft.

Cr-VI.basis_label: element MIGRATION from scraped-off toy material (EN 71-3 Category III, mg/kg of material) — a migration ceiling, not a total-content ceiling
Cr-VI.label: EU Toy Safety Directive hexavalent-chromium migration maximum for Category III (scraped-off) toy material.
Cr-VI.substantiation: The Toy Safety Directive is the only credible sovereign instrument setting a Cr(VI)-specific ceiling for toy material (ASTM F963-17, ISO 8124-3:2020 and NOM-252-SSA1-2011 all regulate TOTAL chromium only, so admitting MX to the credible-regulator set does not add a candidate to this cell; NOM-252's total-chromium rows are named on the Cr cell, never here). Cr(VI) never satisfies the total-chromium cell and the total-chromium screen never satisfies this cell. REACH Annex XVII entry 47 additionally caps Cr(VI) in leather articles at 3 mg/kg on a total-content basis; that content ceiling is a companion obligation for leather components and is not substituted into this migration cell.

toys-balloons.name: Balloons
toys-balloons.native_basis: element migration from scraped-off toy material (Directive 2009/48/EC Annex II Part III point 13, Category III; EN 71-3 / ISO 8124-3 0.07 M HCl 37 C extraction), mg/kg of toy material
toys-balloons.native_basis_label: element MIGRATION from scraped-off toy material (EN 71-3 Category III, mg/kg of material) — a migration ceiling, not a total-content ceiling
toys-balloons.scope_note: Toy balloons: natural-rubber-latex balloons, polychloroprene balloons, metallised-film (foil) balloons, punch balls and water balloons, together with printing, valves and attached ties. Balloons are toys under Directive 2009/48/EC and carry its Annex V Part B choking warning. The balloon wall is a polymeric film tested by scraping/cutting, which is EN 71-3 Category III; the pliable Category I designation is reserved for materials that are ingested as supplied without scraping (modelling and moulding materials), not for elastomer film.
toys-balloons.material: Natural-rubber latex, polychloroprene or metallised polyester/nylon film; surface print; valve; tie.
toys-balloons.components: Separate test portions for balloon wall (per colour), surface print or screen-print, self-sealing valve, and attached tie, ribbon or stick. Mouth-inflated balloons are treated as mouth-contact material for sampling priority.
toys-balloons.audit_scope: toy|children'?s (product|article|jewell?ery)|school.?article|student article|surface coating|accessible part|coated with a material
toys-balloons.basis_guard: ^(element migration from [^;]*toy material \(Category (III)\)|soluble \(migrated\) element from |bioavailable soluble element from )
toys-balloons.basis_guard_note: This row's material is tested by scraping (cured coatings, polymers, elastomers, textiles, wood, paper, glass, ceramic and metal), which is EN 71-3 Category III, so the EU alternative in the guard is pinned to Category III alone. The guard is kind-based on the extraction quantity rather than a literal-phrase whitelist: it admits any register row whose basis BEGINS with element migration from toy material of an admitted material category, with soluble (migrated) element, or with bioavailable soluble element — the three phrasings the EU, US and Mexican migration instruments use for the same 0.07 M HCl acid-extraction quantity — and it will admit a future sovereign migration row phrased differently again only if that row states the same quantity. Anchored at the start of the basis string, it rejects every total-CONTENT phrasing carried in the register (CPSIA total lead content by weight, lead content in accessible part, RoHS homogeneous material, REACH Annex XVII cadmium and organotin content, total cadmium and total lead in children's jewellery, total dry weight of leather, the consumer-textile cadmium restriction, dried-sample and non-volatile coating content, and removable sticker or film content), so no content limit can be resolved into a migration cell. The earlier literal-phrase form was over-restrictive in the one direction that mattered: it refused Mexico's identically-based NOM-252 bioavailable rows even when they were named, and because the guard only fires on ids actually named in a cell, a guard-driven exclusion narrowed the strictest-selection pool silently instead of reporting itself. One soluble-basis register row remains outside the guard on phrasing — Minnesota ch. 347 soluble cadmium in children's jewellery, 75 mg/kg (mn_ch347_2010_cd_childrens_jewelry_75ppm) — and it is neither stricter than any value published on this row nor inside the credible-regulator set (US-MN is a state measure carrying its own federal-supersession caveat).

Pb.basis_label: element MIGRATION from scraped-off toy material (EN 71-3 Category III, mg/kg of material) — a migration ceiling, not a total-content ceiling
Pb.label: Strictest applicable sovereign lead-migration maximum for Category III (scraped-off) toy material, taken across the whole migration family: Directive 2009/48/EC point 13 Category III 23 mg/kg (binding), ASTM F963-17 4.3.5 soluble lead 90 mg/kg (mandatory in the US under CPSIA s.106), and NOM-252-SSA1-2011 Table 1 bioavailable lead 90 mg/kg (MX).
Pb.substantiation: All named ids state one measured quantity — the acid-soluble element that migrates from accessible toy material under the EN 71-3 / ISO 8124-3 0.07 M HCl 37 C extraction, which NOM-252-SSA1-2011 calls bioavailable soluble element — so the strictest-selection is basis-clean. The Directive's Category III value binds at 23 mg/kg; the ASTM and NOM-252 rows are named so the strictest-selection covers the complete applicable family rather than a subset, and both are looser than the binding value. Total-lead CONTENT law runs in parallel on a different basis and is a companion obligation, not this cell's ceiling: CPSIA s.101 caps total lead at 100 mg/kg in any accessible children's-product substrate (cpsia_pb_childrens_product_substrate_100ppm) and at 90 mg/kg in the dried paint film (cpsia_pb_surface_coating_90ppm); Canada SOR/2016-193 and SOR/2011-17 set 90 mg/kg total lead in surface coating material and in applied stickers and films; Canada SOR/2018-83 sets 90 mg/kg total lead in accessible parts. HMTc requires conformity with both the migration ceiling published here and those content ceilings; the two are different measured quantities and are never combined into one number.

Cd.basis_label: element MIGRATION from scraped-off toy material (EN 71-3 Category III, mg/kg of material) — a migration ceiling, not a total-content ceiling
Cd.label: Strictest applicable sovereign cadmium-migration maximum for Category III (scraped-off) toy material, taken across the whole migration family: Directive 2009/48/EC point 13 Category III 17 mg/kg (binding), ASTM F963-17 4.3.5 soluble cadmium 75 mg/kg, and NOM-252-SSA1-2011 Table 1 bioavailable cadmium 75 mg/kg (MX).
Cd.substantiation: All named ids state one measured quantity — the acid-soluble element that migrates from accessible toy material under the EN 71-3 / ISO 8124-3 0.07 M HCl 37 C extraction, which NOM-252-SSA1-2011 calls bioavailable soluble element — so the strictest-selection is basis-clean. The Directive's Category III value binds at 17 mg/kg; the ASTM and NOM-252 rows are named for completeness of the applicable family and are looser. REACH Annex XVII entry 23 as amended by Regulation (EU) 494/2011 restricts cadmium by total CONTENT (0.01 percent in listed polymers and in jewellery metal parts, 0.1 percent in paint and painted articles). Those are content ceilings on a different measured quantity and are far more permissive than the migration ceiling published here; they are recorded as companion obligations and are deliberately NOT used to set this cell, because publishing a 0.1-percent paint-content figure as the HMTc cadmium ceiling would replace a protective migration limit with a permissive content limit.

The earlier literal-phrase form was over-restrictive in the one direction that mattered: it refused Mexico's identically-based NOM-252 bioavailable rows even when they were named, and because the guard only fires on ids actually named in a cell, a guard-driven exclusion narrowed the strictest-selection pool silently instead of reporting itself. Sn.basis_label: element MIGRATION from scraped-off toy material (EN 71-3 Category III, mg/kg of material) — a migration ceiling, not a total-content ceiling

The instrument itself sets TWO tin lines on the same migration basis: total tin (15 000 / 3 750 / 180 000 mg/kg for Categories I / II / III) and organic tin (0.9 / 0.2 / 12 mg/kg), the latter reproduced from the point 13 table on wiki/regulations/eu-2009-48-toy-safety-migration-limits. A prior revision of this cell asserted that the Directive is the only credible sovereign instrument setting a numeric tin ceiling and disclosed only the REACH Annex XVII entry 20 organotin CONTENT restriction; that statement was wrong by omission, because it left the reader unaware that the same instrument caps organic tin at 12 mg/kg for this row's scraped-off (Category III) material while this cell publishes 180 000 mg/kg. Organotin is additionally restricted by REACH Annex XVII entry 20 on a total-CONTENT basis (0.1 percent as tin for dibutyltin, and for skin-contact and childcare articles dioctyltin); that is a different measured quantity and is a further companion obligation, not this cell's anchor.
Sn.screen_note: SCREEN, not a protective standalone ceiling. The published figure is TOTAL tin migration: 180 000 mg/kg of material, which is dominated by benign inorganic tin. Those organic-tin rows are not in data/evidence/regulatory_limits.csv, so no organotin cell can be compiled and none is invented; the total-tin value is therefore recorded as a screen and the organic-tin ceiling is a BINDING PARALLEL OBLIGATION of equal standing, not an optional companion. The total-tin result triggers and bounds organotin determination, never substitutes for it.

toys-marbles.basis_guard_note: This row's material is tested by scraping (cured coatings, polymers, elastomers, textiles, wood, paper, glass, ceramic and metal), which is EN 71-3 Category III, so the EU alternative in the guard is pinned to Category III alone. The guard is kind-based on the extraction quantity rather than a literal-phrase whitelist: it admits any register row whose basis BEGINS with element migration from toy material of an admitted material category, with soluble (migrated) element, or with bioavailable soluble element — the three phrasings the EU, US and Mexican migration instruments use for the same 0.07 M HCl acid-extraction quantity — and it will admit a future sovereign migration row phrased differently again only if that row states the same quantity. Anchored at the start of the basis string, it rejects every total-CONTENT phrasing carried in the register (CPSIA total lead content by weight, lead content in accessible part, RoHS homogeneous material, REACH Annex XVII cadmium and organotin content, total cadmium and total lead in children's jewellery, total dry weight of leather, the consumer-textile cadmium restriction, dried-sample and non-volatile coating content, and removable sticker or film content), so no content limit can be resolved into a migration cell. The earlier literal-phrase form was over-restrictive in the one direction that mattered: it refused Mexico's identically-based NOM-252 bioavailable rows even when they were named, and because the guard only fires on ids actually named in a cell, a guard-driven exclusion narrowed the strictest-selection pool silently instead of reporting itself. One soluble-basis register row remains outside the guard on phrasing — Minnesota ch. 347 soluble cadmium in children's jewellery, 75 mg/kg (mn_ch347_2010_cd_childrens_jewelry_75ppm) — and it is neither stricter than any value published on this row nor inside the credible-regulator set (US-MN is a state measure carrying its own federal-supersession caveat).

A prior revision of this cell asserted that the Directive is the only credible sovereign instrument setting a numeric tin ceiling and disclosed only the REACH Annex XVII entry 20 organotin CONTENT restriction; that statement was wrong by omission, because it left the reader unaware that the same instrument caps organic tin at 12 mg/kg for this row's scraped-off (Category III) material while this cell publishes 180 000 mg/kg. The organic-tin migration rows are a recorded REGISTER GAP returned for ingestion through the verified regulatory-fetch pathway; once ingested, this row should gain a published organotin cell beside the total-tin screen, exactly as chromium carries a published Cr(VI) cell beside its total-chromium screen. Organotin is additionally restricted by REACH Annex XVII entry 20 on a total-CONTENT basis (0.1 percent as tin for dibutyltin, and for skin-contact and childcare articles dioctyltin); that is a different measured quantity and is a further companion obligation, not this cell's anchor.
Sn.screen_note: SCREEN, not a protective standalone ceiling. The published figure is TOTAL tin migration: 180 000 mg/kg of material, which is dominated by benign inorganic tin. The health-relevant tin fraction is organotin, and the SAME instrument on the SAME migration basis (Directive 2009/48/EC Annex II Part III point 13) sets a separate organic-tin migration ceiling of 0.9 mg/kg for Category I, 0.2 mg/kg for Category II and 12 mg/kg for Category III — for this row's scraped-off (Category III) material that is 12 mg/kg, orders of magnitude below the total-tin figure. Those organic-tin rows are not in data/evidence/regulatory_limits.csv, so no organotin cell can be compiled and none is invented; the total-tin value is therefore recorded as a screen and the organic-tin ceiling is a BINDING PARALLEL OBLIGATION of equal standing, not an optional companion. The total-tin result triggers and bounds organotin determination, never substitutes for it.

Al.basis_label: element MIGRATION from scraped-off toy material (EN 71-3 Category III, mg/kg of material) — a migration ceiling, not a total-content ceiling
Al.label: EU Toy Safety Directive aluminium migration maximum for Category III (scraped-off) toy material (as amended by Directive (EU) 2019/1922).
Al.substantiation: The Toy Safety Directive is the only credible sovereign instrument setting a numeric aluminium ceiling for toy material; ASTM F963-17 and ISO 8124-3:2020 do not regulate aluminium, and NOM-252-SSA1-2011 Table 1 regulates antimony, arsenic, barium, cadmium, total chromium, lead, mercury and selenium and sets no aluminium limit, so admitting MX to the credible-regulator set does not add a candidate to this cell. The 2019/1922 amendment already tightened these values by roughly 2.5x; HMTc publishes the amended figures as written.

Cr.basis_label: acid-soluble / MIGRATED element from accessible toy material (EN 71-3 / ISO 8124-3 0.07 M HCl, 37 C, mg/kg of material). The three instruments in this family state the same measured quantity in three phrasings: Directive 2009/48/EC point 13 element migration, which IS split by material category and whose applicable member here is the Category III (scraped-off material) value; ASTM F963-17 4.3.5 soluble (migrated) element; and NOM-252-SSA1-2011 bioavailable soluble element. The ASTM and NOM-252 limits are not EN 71-3 material-category scoped, so where one of them binds, the published ceiling carries no material-category qualifier. A migration ceiling, not a total-content ceiling.
Cr.screen_note: SCREEN, not a protective standalone ceiling. Total chromium in toy material is dominated by benign Cr(III) from pigments, stainless components and tanned leather; the health-relevant species is Cr(VI), which carries its own published cell on this row. Cr.label: Total-chromium migration maximum taken over the two credible sovereign instruments that set one on this basis: ASTM F963-17 4.3.5 soluble total chromium 60 mg/kg (mandatory in the US under CPSIA s.106) and NOM-252-SSA1-2011 Table 1 bioavailable total chromium 60 mg/kg for toy or school-article material other than modelling clay and finger paint (MX). Both agree at 60 mg/kg. Recorded as a SCREEN, not a protective standalone ceiling.
Cr.substantiation: The EU Toy Safety Directive splits chromium into Cr(III) and Cr(VI) and sets no TOTAL-chromium ceiling, so the total-chromium value is taken over the two credible sovereign instruments that do set one on the acid-soluble migration basis. AUDIT ANSWER — NOM-252 PRESCHOOL TIER. The audit scan flags NOM-252-SSA1-2011's stricter chromium tier (25 mg/kg, mx_nom252_2011_cr_total_preschool_clay_fingerpaint_25) as unselected. toys-yo-yo-elastic-tether.name: Yo-yo elastic tether toys

toys-yo-yo-elastic-tether.components: Separate test portions for tether elastomer or elasticated cord, body polymer (per colour), finger loop, any internal fill or gel, and printed decoration. An accessible internal liquid or gel routes to toys-crafts-other, which publishes the Category II ceilings.
toys-yo-yo-elastic-tether.audit_scope: toy|children'?s (product|article|jewell?ery)|school.?article|student article|surface coating|accessible part|coated with a material
toys-yo-yo-elastic-tether.basis_guard: ^(element migration from [^;]*toy material \(Category (III)\)|soluble \(migrated\) element from |bioavailable soluble element from )
toys-yo-yo-elastic-tether.basis_guard_note: This row's material is tested by scraping (cured coatings, polymers, elastomers, textiles, wood, paper, glass, ceramic and metal), which is EN 71-3 Category III, so the EU alternative in the guard is pinned to Category III alone. The guard is kind-based on the extraction quantity rather than a literal-phrase whitelist: it admits any register row whose basis BEGINS with element migration from toy material of an admitted material category, with soluble (migrated) element, or with bioavailable soluble element — the three phrasings the EU, US and Mexican migration instruments use for the same 0.07 M HCl acid-extraction quantity — and it will admit a future sovereign migration row phrased differently again only if that row states the same quantity. Anchored at the start of the basis string, it rejects every total-CONTENT phrasing carried in the register (CPSIA total lead content by weight, lead content in accessible part, RoHS homogeneous material, REACH Annex XVII cadmium and organotin content, total cadmium and total lead in children's jewellery, total dry weight of leather, the consumer-textile cadmium restriction, dried-sample and non-volatile coating content, and removable sticker or film content), so no content limit can be resolved into a migration cell. The earlier literal-phrase form was over-restrictive in the one direction that mattered: it refused Mexico's identically-based NOM-252 bioavailable rows even when they were named, and because the guard only fires on ids actually named in a cell, a guard-driven exclusion narrowed the strictest-selection pool silently instead of reporting itself. One soluble-basis register row remains outside the guard on phrasing — Minnesota ch. 347 soluble cadmium in children's jewellery, 75 mg/kg (mn_ch347_2010_cd_childrens_jewelry_75ppm) — and it is neither stricter than any value published on this row nor inside the credible-regulator set (US-MN is a state measure carrying its own federal-supersession caveat).

Pb.basis_label: element MIGRATION from scraped-off toy material (EN 71-3 Category III, mg/kg of material) — a migration ceiling, not a total-content ceiling
Pb.label: Strictest applicable sovereign lead-migration maximum for Category III (scraped-off) toy material, taken across the whole migration family: Directive 2009/48/EC point 13 Category III 23 mg/kg (binding), ASTM F963-17 4.3.5 soluble lead 90 mg/kg (mandatory in the US under CPSIA s.106), and NOM-252-SSA1-2011 Table 1 bioavailable lead 90 mg/kg (MX).
Pb.substantiation: All named ids state one measured quantity — the acid-soluble element that migrates from accessible toy material under the EN 71-3 / ISO 8124-3 0.07 M HCl 37 C extraction, which NOM-252-SSA1-2011 calls bioavailable soluble element — so the strictest-selection is basis-clean. The Directive's Category III value binds at 23 mg/kg; the ASTM and NOM-252 rows are named so the strictest-selection covers the complete applicable family rather than a subset, and both are looser than the binding value. Total-lead CONTENT law runs in parallel on a different basis and is a companion obligation, not this cell's ceiling: CPSIA s.101 caps total lead at 100 mg/kg in any accessible children's-product substrate (cpsia_pb_childrens_product_substrate_100ppm) and at 90 mg/kg in the dried paint film (cpsia_pb_surface_coating_90ppm); Canada SOR/2016-193 and SOR/2011-17 set 90 mg/kg total lead in surface coating material and in applied stickers and films; Canada SOR/2018-83 sets 90 mg/kg total lead in accessible parts. HMTc requires conformity with both the migration ceiling published here and those content ceilings; the two are different measured quantities and are never combined into one number.

THAT ARGUMENT IS WITHDRAWN AS UNSUBSTANTIATED. The only repository artifact cited for it, wiki/sources/iso2020-8124-3-toy-migration-elements.md, documents the Table 2 analytical correction for ISO 8124-3:2020 and says of ASTM only that F963 4.3 sits in the same lineage and used the legacy EN 71-3 limits unchanged through F963-07 — a limit-VALUE lineage statement that expressly ends before the F963-08 and later editions this cell relies on, and it attributes no analytical correction to ASTM at all. not_material.rationale: No sovereign toy-safety instrument sets an inorganic-arsenic limit. not_material.reference_method: Total-arsenic migration on this row's EN 71-3 material category (0.07 M HCl, 37 C, 1 h agitation + 1 h standing, 0.45 um filtration, ICP-MS). No reflex arsenic speciation is defined for toy materials; HMTc requires a reflex investigation of the arsenic source whenever total-arsenic migration exceeds 50 percent of the published ceiling.

NOM-252-SSA1-2011 Table 1 (arsenic, total element, both scope tiers), mandatory in Mexico since 2012-08-13. None of the four speciates arsenic.
not_material.jurisdictions_checked: EU (2009/48/EC as amended), UK (retained TSD / Toys (Safety) Regulations 2011), US (CPSIA s.106 / 16 CFR 1250 / ASTM F963-17), CA (SOR/2011-17, SOR/2016-193, SOR/2018-83), AU-NZ, CODEX, MX (NOM-252-SSA1-2011), international (ISO 8124-3:2020)

Cr.basis_label: acid-soluble / MIGRATED element from accessible toy material (EN 71-3 / ISO 8124-3 0.07 M HCl, 37 C, mg/kg of material). The three instruments in this family state the same measured quantity in three phrasings: Directive 2009/48/EC point 13 element migration, which IS split by material category and whose applicable member here is the Category III (scraped-off material) value; ASTM F963-17 4.3.5 soluble (migrated) element; and NOM-252-SSA1-2011 bioavailable soluble element. The ASTM and NOM-252 limits are not EN 71-3 material-category scoped, so where one of them binds, the published ceiling carries no material-category qualifier. A migration ceiling, not a total-content ceiling.
Cr.screen_note: SCREEN, not a protective standalone ceiling. Total chromium in toy material is dominated by benign Cr(III) from pigments, stainless components and tanned leather; the health-relevant species is Cr(VI), which carries its own published cell on this row. The total-chromium result is used to trigger and to bound Cr(VI) speciation, never as a substitute for it.
Cr.label: Total-chromium migration maximum taken over the two credible sovereign instruments that set one on this basis: ASTM F963-17 4.3.5 soluble total chromium 60 mg/kg (mandatory in the US under CPSIA s.106) and NOM-252-SSA1-2011 Table 1 bioavailable total chromium 60 mg/kg for toy or school-article material other than modelling clay and finger paint (MX). Both agree at 60 mg/kg. Recorded as a SCREEN, not a protective standalone ceiling.
Cr.substantiation: The EU Toy Safety Directive splits chromium into Cr(III) and Cr(VI) and sets no TOTAL-chromium ceiling, so the total-chromium value is taken over the two credible sovereign instruments that do set one on the acid-soluble migration basis. ASTM F963-17 and NOM-252-SSA1-2011 agree at 60 mg/kg and HMTc applies that figure to the laboratory's analytical result as reported. NOM-252's stricter 25 mg/kg tier is scoped to preschool school articles, modelling clay and finger paint; none of those material forms is within this row's scope, so that tier is inapplicable here and it binds instead on art-craft-materials and toys-crafts-other, whose scopes name modelling clay, dough and finger paint expressly. TWO PRIOR STATEMENTS ON THIS CELL ARE WITHDRAWN. First, the assertion that ASTM applies a 30 percent analytical correction raising its enforced ceiling to about 86 mg/kg, so that HMTc's use of the nominal 60 mg/kg was over-compliance: that reading is unsubstantiated for the F963 editions relied on, for the reason recorded on the tAs cell, and 60 mg/kg is simply the instrument's figure applied as written. Second, the claim that the ISO 8124-3:2020 modelling-clay and finger-paint chromium limits of 25 mg/kg were a register gap: the same 25 mg/kg value for the same two material forms IS in the register as the Mexican statutory row mx_nom252_2011_cr_total_preschool_clay_fingerpaint_25, and it now binds the rows it applies to. One genuine register gap remains against this cell and is recorded rather than worked around: the EU Cr(III) migration rows of Directive 2009/48/EC point 13 are absent from the register (verified — no Cr-III species exists anywhere in it) and are not invented here. AUDIT ANSWER — NOM-252 PRESCHOOL TIER. The audit scan flags NOM-252-SSA1-2011's stricter chromium tier (25 mg/kg, mx_nom252_2011_cr_total_preschool_clay_fingerpaint_25) as unselected. It is inapplicable to this row for the reason stated above — the tier is scoped to preschool school articles, modelling clay and finger paint, none of which is within this row's scope — and it IS adopted on the three rows whose material forms fall inside it: art-craft-materials, toys-crafts-other and toys-pompoms-fibrous-craft.

Cr-VI.basis_label: element MIGRATION from scraped-off toy material (EN 71-3 Category III, mg/kg of material) — a migration ceiling, not a total-content ceiling

Cr(VI) never satisfies the total-chromium cell and the total-chromium screen never satisfies this cell. REACH Annex XVII entry 47 additionally caps Cr(VI) in leather articles at 3 mg/kg on a total-content basis; that content ceiling is a companion obligation for leather components and is not substituted into this migration cell.

toys-pompoms-fibrous-craft.name: Pompoms and similar small fibrous craft items
toys-pompoms-fibrous-craft.native_basis: element migration from scraped-off toy material (Directive 2009/48/EC Annex II Part III point 13, Category III; EN 71-3 / ISO 8124-3 0.07 M HCl 37 C extraction), mg/kg of toy material
toys-pompoms-fibrous-craft.native_basis_label: element MIGRATION from scraped-off toy material (EN 71-3 Category III, mg/kg of material) — a migration ceiling, not a total-content ceiling
toys-pompoms-fibrous-craft.scope_note: Small fibrous craft components: pompoms, chenille stems and pipe cleaners, felt shapes, yarn, craft feathers, raffia, googly-eye backing felt and similar loose craft items. Dyes and dye auxiliaries are the metals risk on this row. Textile fibre is tested by cutting/scraping, which is EN 71-3 Category III.
toys-pompoms-fibrous-craft.material: Dyed acrylic, polyester, wool or cotton fibre; chenille stem wire core; felt; dyed feather; raffia.
toys-pompoms-fibrous-craft.components: Separate test portions per fibre type and per dye colour, plus the chenille stem wire core and any metallic or glitter-coated fibre tested separately. Deeply saturated reds, oranges and yellows are prioritised for sampling because those shades carry the highest historical metal-complex dye loading.
toys-pompoms-fibrous-craft.audit_scope: toy|children'?s (product|article|jewell?ery)|school.?article|student article|surface coating|accessible part|coated with a material
toys-pompoms-fibrous-craft.basis_guard: ^(element migration from [^;]*toy material \(Category (III)\)|soluble \(migrated\) element from |bioavailable soluble element from )
toys-pompoms-fibrous-craft.basis_guard_note: This row's material is tested by scraping (cured coatings, polymers, elastomers, textiles, wood, paper, glass, ceramic and metal), which is EN 71-3 Category III, so the EU alternative in the guard is pinned to Category III alone. The guard is kind-based on the extraction quantity rather than a literal-phrase whitelist: it admits any register row whose basis BEGINS with element migration from toy material of an admitted material category, with soluble (migrated) element, or with bioavailable soluble element — the three phrasings the EU, US and Mexican migration instruments use for the same 0.07 M HCl acid-extraction quantity — and it will admit a future sovereign migration row phrased differently again only if that row states the same quantity. Anchored at the start of the basis string, it rejects every total-CONTENT phrasing carried in the register (CPSIA total lead content by weight, lead content in accessible part, RoHS homogeneous material, REACH Annex XVII cadmium and organotin content, total cadmium and total lead in children's jewellery, total dry weight of leather, the consumer-textile cadmium restriction, dried-sample and non-volatile coating content, and removable sticker or film content), so no content limit can be resolved into a migration cell. The earlier literal-phrase form was over-restrictive in the one direction that mattered: it refused Mexico's identically-based NOM-252 bioavailable rows even when they were named, and because the guard only fires on ids actually named in a cell, a guard-driven exclusion narrowed the strictest-selection pool silently instead of reporting itself. One soluble-basis register row remains outside the guard on phrasing — Minnesota ch. 347 soluble cadmium in children's jewellery, 75 mg/kg (mn_ch347_2010_cd_childrens_jewelry_75ppm) — and it is neither stricter than any value published on this row nor inside the credible-regulator set (US-MN is a state measure carrying its own federal-supersession caveat).

Pb.basis_label: element MIGRATION from scraped-off toy material (EN 71-3 Category III, mg/kg of material) — a migration ceiling, not a total-content ceiling
Pb.label: Strictest applicable sovereign lead-migration maximum for Category III (scraped-off) toy material, taken across the whole migration family: Directive 2009/48/EC point 13 Category III 23 mg/kg (binding), ASTM F963-17 4.3.5 soluble lead 90 mg/kg (mandatory in the US under CPSIA s.106), and NOM-252-SSA1-2011 Table 1 bioavailable lead 90 mg/kg (MX).
Pb.substantiation: All named ids state one measured quantity — the acid-soluble element that migrates from accessible toy material under the EN 71-3 / ISO 8124-3 0.07 M HCl 37 C extraction, which NOM-252-SSA1-2011 calls bioavailable soluble element — so the strictest-selection is basis-clean. The Directive's Category III value binds at 23 mg/kg; the ASTM and NOM-252 rows are named so the strictest-selection covers the complete applicable family rather than a subset, and both are looser than the binding value. Total-lead CONTENT law runs in parallel on a different basis and is a companion obligation, not this cell's ceiling: CPSIA s.101 caps total lead at 100 mg/kg in any accessible children's-product substrate (cpsia_pb_childrens_product_substrate_100ppm) and at 90 mg/kg in the dried paint film (cpsia_pb_surface_coating_90ppm); Canada SOR/2016-193 and SOR/2011-17 set 90 mg/kg total lead in surface coating material and in applied stickers and films; Canada SOR/2018-83 sets 90 mg/kg total lead in accessible parts. HMTc requires conformity with both the migration ceiling published here and those content ceilings; the two are different measured quantities and are never combined into one number. This row's material — pompoms, chenille stems and pipe cleaners, felt shapes, yarn, craft feathers, raffia and similar loose fibrous craft components — is supplied as preschool school-craft material, so NOM-252-SSA1-2011's preschool school-article tier is directly applicable and is adopted alongside its general tier. Where the two tiers differ the stricter binds. Deciding the other way would require arguing that a craft pompom sold into preschool use is not a school article; HMTc does not take that position, and the protective reading costs nothing. Both NOM-252 lead tiers set 90 mg/kg, so the tier question does not move this cell; the Directive's Category III value of 23 mg/kg still binds.

Cd.basis_label: element MIGRATION from scraped-off toy material (EN 71-3 Category III, mg/kg of material) — a migration ceiling, not a total-content ceiling
Cd.label: Strictest applicable sovereign cadmium-migration maximum for Category III (scraped-off) toy material, taken across the whole migration family: Directive 2009/48/EC point 13 Category III 17 mg/kg (binding), ASTM F963-17 4.3.5 soluble cadmium 75 mg/kg, and NOM-252-SSA1-2011 Table 1 bioavailable cadmium 75 mg/kg (MX).

Those are content ceilings on a different measured quantity and are far more permissive than the migration ceiling published here; they are recorded as companion obligations and are deliberately NOT used to set this cell, because publishing a 0.1-percent paint-content figure as the HMTc cadmium ceiling would replace a protective migration limit with a permissive content limit. This row's material — pompoms, chenille stems and pipe cleaners, felt shapes, yarn, craft feathers, raffia and similar loose fibrous craft components — is supplied as preschool school-craft material, so NOM-252-SSA1-2011's preschool school-article tier is directly applicable and is adopted alongside its general tier. Deciding the other way would require arguing that a craft pompom sold into preschool use is not a school article; HMTc does not take that position, and the protective reading costs nothing. THAT ARGUMENT IS WITHDRAWN AS UNSUBSTANTIATED. HMTc does not publish a ceiling above a figure made mandatory by CPSIA s.106 / 16 CFR 1250 on an unsubstantiated reading of a conformity clause. Both NOM-252 arsenic tiers set 25 mg/kg, which is the binding value here in any event.

not_material.rationale: No sovereign toy-safety instrument sets an inorganic-arsenic limit. NOM-252-SSA1-2011 Table 1 (arsenic, total element, both scope tiers), mandatory in Mexico since 2012-08-13. None of the four speciates arsenic.
not_material.jurisdictions_checked: EU (2009/48/EC as amended), UK (retained TSD / Toys (Safety) Regulations 2011), US (CPSIA s.106 / 16 CFR 1250 / ASTM F963-17), CA (SOR/2011-17, SOR/2016-193, SOR/2018-83), AU-NZ, CODEX, MX (NOM-252-SSA1-2011), international (ISO 8124-3:2020)

not_material.rationale: Methylmercury is produced by microbial methylation in aquatic systems and reaches humans by diet. a dyed textile fibre, chenille stem, felt piece or feather carries no methylation pathway and no dietary route, and no sovereign toy instrument sets a methylmercury limit: every toy mercury limit (2009/48/EC point 13, ASTM F963-17 4.3.5, ISO 8124-3:2020, NOM-252-SSA1-2011, Canada SOR/2011-17 and SOR/2016-193) is on total mercury. Ni.basis_label: element MIGRATION from scraped-off toy material (EN 71-3 Category III, mg/kg of material) — a migration ceiling, not a total-content ceiling
Ni.label: EU Toy Safety Directive nickel migration maximum for Category III (scraped-off) toy material.
Ni.substantiation: The Toy Safety Directive is the only credible sovereign instrument that sets a numeric nickel ceiling for toy material; ASTM F963-17 and ISO 8124-3:2020 do not regulate nickel at all, and NOM-252-SSA1-2011 Table 1 regulates antimony, arsenic, barium, cadmium, total chromium, lead, mercury and selenium and sets no nickel limit, so admitting MX to the credible-regulator set does not add a candidate to this cell. The Directive's nickel figures are permissive relative to the other panel analytes and HMTc publishes them as written rather than substituting an occurrence-derived or invented value. REACH Annex XVII entry 27 additionally caps nickel RELEASE from articles in prolonged skin contact at 0.5 ug/cm2/week; that is a per-area release rate in a third basis, it is not represented in the register, and it is recorded as a companion obligation and a register gap rather than converted into a mg/kg figure here.

Sn.basis_label: element MIGRATION from scraped-off toy material (EN 71-3 Category III, mg/kg of material) — a migration ceiling, not a total-content ceiling
Sn.label: EU Toy Safety Directive TOTAL-tin migration maximum for Category III (scraped-off) toy material, recorded as a SCREEN; the same instrument's organic-tin migration ceiling for Category III material, 12 mg/kg, is a binding parallel obligation pending register ingestion.
Sn.substantiation: Directive 2009/48/EC Annex II Part III point 13 is the only instrument in the register that sets a numeric tin ceiling for toy material: ASTM F963-17 and ISO 8124-3:2020 do not regulate tin, and NOM-252-SSA1-2011 Table 1 regulates antimony, arsenic, barium, cadmium, total chromium, lead, mercury and selenium and sets no tin limit, so admitting MX to the credible-regulator set does not add a candidate to this cell. The register holds only the Directive's three TOTAL-tin rows. The instrument itself sets TWO tin lines on the same migration basis: total tin (15 000 / 3 750 / 180 000 mg/kg for Categories I / II / III) and organic tin (0.9 / 0.2 / 12 mg/kg), the latter reproduced from the point 13 table on wiki/regulations/eu-2009-48-toy-safety-migration-limits. A prior revision of this cell asserted that the Directive is the only credible sovereign instrument setting a numeric tin ceiling and disclosed only the REACH Annex XVII entry 20 organotin CONTENT restriction; that statement was wrong by omission, because it left the reader unaware that the same instrument caps organic tin at 12 mg/kg for this row's scraped-off (Category III) material while this cell publishes 180 000 mg/kg. The organic-tin migration rows are a recorded REGISTER GAP returned for ingestion through the verified regulatory-fetch pathway; once ingested, this row should gain a published organotin cell beside the total-tin screen, exactly as chromium carries a published Cr(VI) cell beside its total-chromium screen. Organotin is additionally restricted by REACH Annex XVII entry 20 on a total-CONTENT basis (0.1 percent as tin for dibutyltin, and for skin-contact and childcare articles dioctyltin); that is a different measured quantity and is a further companion obligation, not this cell's anchor.
Sn.screen_note: SCREEN, not a protective standalone ceiling. The published figure is TOTAL tin migration: 180 000 mg/kg of material, which is dominated by benign inorganic tin. The health-relevant tin fraction is organotin, and the SAME instrument on the SAME migration basis (Directive 2009/48/EC Annex II Part III point 13) sets a separate organic-tin migration ceiling of 0.9 mg/kg for Category I, 0.2 mg/kg for Category II and 12 mg/kg for Category III — for this row's scraped-off (Category III) material that is 12 mg/kg, orders of magnitude below the total-tin figure. Those organic-tin rows are not in data/evidence/regulatory_limits.csv, so no organotin cell can be compiled and none is invented; the total-tin value is therefore recorded as a screen and the organic-tin ceiling is a BINDING PARALLEL OBLIGATION of equal standing, not an optional companion. The total-tin result triggers and bounds organotin determination, never substitutes for it.

Recorded as a SCREEN, not a protective standalone ceiling.
Cr.substantiation: The EU Toy Safety Directive splits chromium into Cr(III) and Cr(VI) and sets no TOTAL-chromium ceiling, so the total-chromium value is taken over the two credible sovereign instruments that do set one on the acid-soluble migration basis. ASTM F963-17 and the NOM-252 general tier agree at 60 mg/kg, and NOM-252's preschool school-article tier is stricter at 25 mg/kg. This row's material — pompoms, chenille stems and pipe cleaners, felt shapes, yarn, craft feathers, raffia and similar loose fibrous craft components — is supplied as preschool school-craft material, so NOM-252-SSA1-2011's preschool school-article tier is directly applicable and is adopted alongside its general tier. Where the two tiers differ the stricter binds. Deciding the other way would require arguing that a craft pompom sold into preschool use is not a school article; HMTc does not take that position, and the protective reading costs nothing. NOM-252's preschool school-article tier therefore binds this cell at 25 mg/kg, below the 60 mg/kg that ASTM F963-17 and the NOM-252 general tier set. TWO PRIOR STATEMENTS ON THIS CELL ARE WITHDRAWN. First, the assertion that ASTM applies a 30 percent analytical correction raising its enforced ceiling to about 86 mg/kg, so that HMTc's use of the nominal 60 mg/kg was over-compliance: that reading is unsubstantiated for the F963 editions relied on, for the reason recorded on the tAs cell, and 60 mg/kg is simply the instrument's figure applied as written. Second, the claim that the ISO 8124-3:2020 modelling-clay and finger-paint chromium limits of 25 mg/kg were a register gap: the same 25 mg/kg value for the same two material forms IS in the register as the Mexican statutory row mx_nom252_2011_cr_total_preschool_clay_fingerpaint_25, and it now binds the rows it applies to. One genuine register gap remains against this cell and is recorded rather than worked around: the EU Cr(III) migration rows of Directive 2009/48/EC point 13 are absent from the register (verified — no Cr-III species exists anywhere in it) and are not invented here.

Cr-VI.basis_label: element MIGRATION from scraped-off toy material (EN 71-3 Category III, mg/kg of material) — a migration ceiling, not a total-content ceiling
Cr-VI.label: EU Toy Safety Directive hexavalent-chromium migration maximum for Category III (scraped-off) toy material.
Cr-VI.substantiation: The Toy Safety Directive is the only credible sovereign instrument setting a Cr(VI)-specific ceiling for toy material (ASTM F963-17, ISO 8124-3:2020 and NOM-252-SSA1-2011 all regulate TOTAL chromium only, so admitting MX to the credible-regulator set does not add a candidate to this cell; NOM-252's total-chromium rows are named on the Cr cell, never here). Cr(VI) never satisfies the total-chromium cell and the total-chromium screen never satisfies this cell. REACH Annex XVII entry 47 additionally caps Cr(VI) in leather articles at 3 mg/kg on a total-content basis; that content ceiling is a companion obligation for leather components and is not substituted into this migration cell.

toys-attached-cribs-playpens.name: Toys attached to cribs/playpens
toys-attached-cribs-playpens.native_basis: element migration from scraped-off toy material (Directive 2009/48/EC Annex II Part III point 13, Category III; EN 71-3 / ISO 8124-3 0.07 M HCl 37 C extraction), mg/kg of toy material
toys-attached-cribs-playpens.native_basis_label: element MIGRATION from scraped-off toy material (EN 71-3 Category III, mg/kg of material) — a migration ceiling, not a total-content ceiling
toys-attached-cribs-playpens.scope_note: Toys designed to be attached to a crib, cot, playpen or play yard: mobiles, activity panels, crib gyms, attached mirrors and hanging figures, together with their attachment straps, clamps and cords. These toys are within reach of an infant for prolonged unsupervised periods and are heavily mouthed. Cord and strap length requirements under EN 71-1 and ASTM F963-17 are mechanical and are not converted into a metals number. Teethers attached to the same frame are HMTc Category 9.
toys-attached-cribs-playpens.material: Polymer figures and panels; textile and plush elements; mirror backing; attachment strap, clamp and cord.
toys-attached-cribs-playpens.components: Separate test portions for figure and panel polymer (per colour), applied coating, textile and plush elements, mirror backing and frame, attachment strap webbing, clamp polymer, and any metal fastener or spring. The crib, cot or play yard itself is a durable nursery product outside Category 21.
toys-attached-cribs-playpens.audit_scope: toy|children'?s (product|article|jewell?ery)|school.?article|student article|surface coating|accessible part|coated with a material
toys-attached-cribs-playpens.basis_guard: ^(element migration from [^;]*toy material \(Category (III)\)|soluble \(migrated\) element from |bioavailable soluble element from )
toys-attached-cribs-playpens.basis_guard_note: This row's material is tested by scraping (cured coatings, polymers, elastomers, textiles, wood, paper, glass, ceramic and metal), which is EN 71-3 Category III, so the EU alternative in the guard is pinned to Category III alone. The guard is kind-based on the extraction quantity rather than a literal-phrase whitelist: it admits any register row whose basis BEGINS with element migration from toy material of an admitted material category, with soluble (migrated) element, or with bioavailable soluble element — the three phrasings the EU, US and Mexican migration instruments use for the same 0.07 M HCl acid-extraction quantity — and it will admit a future sovereign migration row phrased differently again only if that row states the same quantity. Anchored at the start of the basis string, it rejects every total-CONTENT phrasing carried in the register (CPSIA total lead content by weight, lead content in accessible part, RoHS homogeneous material, REACH Annex XVII cadmium and organotin content, total cadmium and total lead in children's jewellery, total dry weight of leather, the consumer-textile cadmium restriction, dried-sample and non-volatile coating content, and removable sticker or film content), so no content limit can be resolved into a migration cell. The earlier literal-phrase form was over-restrictive in the one direction that mattered: it refused Mexico's identically-based NOM-252 bioavailable rows even when they were named, and because the guard only fires on ids actually named in a cell, a guard-driven exclusion narrowed the strictest-selection pool silently instead of reporting itself. One soluble-basis register row remains outside the guard on phrasing — Minnesota ch. 347 soluble cadmium in children's jewellery, 75 mg/kg (mn_ch347_2010_cd_childrens_jewelry_75ppm) — and it is neither stricter than any value published on this row nor inside the credible-regulator set (US-MN is a state measure carrying its own federal-supersession caveat).
toys-attached-cribs-playpens.cross_reference: Teethers and teething toys attached to a crib or play-yard frame are HMTc Category 9 (Infant and Child Contact Products). The crib, cot or play yard itself is a durable nursery product and is not certified on this row.

Pb.basis_label: element MIGRATION from scraped-off toy material (EN 71-3 Category III, mg/kg of material) — a migration ceiling, not a total-content ceiling
Pb.label: Strictest applicable sovereign lead-migration maximum for Category III (scraped-off) toy material, taken across the whole migration family: Directive 2009/48/EC point 13 Category III 23 mg/kg (binding), ASTM F963-17 4.3.5 soluble lead 90 mg/kg (mandatory in the US under CPSIA s.106), and NOM-252-SSA1-2011 Table 1 bioavailable lead 90 mg/kg (MX).
Pb.substantiation: All named ids state one measured quantity — the acid-soluble element that migrates from accessible toy material under the EN 71-3 / ISO 8124-3 0.07 M HCl 37 C extraction, which NOM-252-SSA1-2011 calls bioavailable soluble element — so the strictest-selection is basis-clean. The Directive's Category III value binds at 23 mg/kg; the ASTM and NOM-252 rows are named so the strictest-selection covers the complete applicable family rather than a subset, and both are looser than the binding value. Total-lead CONTENT law runs in parallel on a different basis and is a companion obligation, not this cell's ceiling: CPSIA s.101 caps total lead at 100 mg/kg in any accessible children's-product substrate (cpsia_pb_childrens_product_substrate_100ppm) and at 90 mg/kg in the dried paint film (cpsia_pb_surface_coating_90ppm); Canada SOR/2016-193 and SOR/2011-17 set 90 mg/kg total lead in surface coating material and in applied stickers and films; Canada SOR/2018-83 sets 90 mg/kg total lead in accessible parts. HMTc requires conformity with both the migration ceiling published here and those content ceilings; the two are different measured quantities and are never combined into one number.

The Directive's Category III value binds at 17 mg/kg; the ASTM and NOM-252 rows are named for completeness of the applicable family and are looser. REACH Annex XVII entry 23 as amended by Regulation (EU) 494/2011 restricts cadmium by total CONTENT (0.01 percent in listed polymers and in jewellery metal parts, 0.1 percent in paint and painted articles). tAs.basis_label: acid-soluble / MIGRATED element from accessible toy material (EN 71-3 / ISO 8124-3 0.07 M HCl, 37 C, mg/kg of material). The three instruments in this family state the same measured quantity in three phrasings: Directive 2009/48/EC point 13 element migration, which IS split by material category and whose applicable member here is the Category III (scraped-off material) value; ASTM F963-17 4.3.5 soluble (migrated) element; and NOM-252-SSA1-2011 bioavailable soluble element. A migration ceiling, not a total-content ceiling.
tAs.label: Strictest applicable sovereign total-arsenic migration maximum for Category III (scraped-off) toy material, taken across the whole migration family: ASTM F963-17 4.3.5 soluble arsenic 25 mg/kg (mandatory in the US under CPSIA s.106 / 16 CFR 1250) and NOM-252-SSA1-2011 Table 1 bioavailable arsenic 25 mg/kg (MX) both bind at 25 mg/kg, below the Directive's point 13 Category III value of 47 mg/kg.
